title.en: Volume 357 Biographies 144: Wu Xiongguang, Wang Zhiyi, Chen Dawen, Xiong Mei, Qiu Xingjian, Fang Weidian, Dong Jiaozeng
title.raw: 卷357 列傳一百四十四 吴熊光 汪志伊 陈大文 熊枚 裘行简 方维甸 董教增

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 144
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 144

sentences.zh: 吳熊光汪志伊陳大文熊枚裘行簡

translations.literal: Wu Xiongguang, Wang Zhiyi, Chen Dawen, Xiong Mei, and Qiu Xingjian
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiongguang, Wang Zhiyi, Chen Dawen, Xiong Mei, and Qiu Xingjian

sentences.zh: 方維甸董教增

translations.literal: Fang Weidian and Dong Jiaozeng
translations.idiomatic: Fang Weidian and Dong Jiaozeng

sentences.zh: 吳熊光，字槐江，江蘇昭文人。

translations.literal: Wu Xiongguang, style name Huaijiang, was a native of Zhaowen in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiongguang, styled Huaijiang, was from Zhaowen in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 舉順天鄉試，乾隆三十七年，登中正榜，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination; in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong he was listed on the secondary quota, was appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination, and in the thirty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign he placed on the secondary quota, received appointment as a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部郎中，改御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to director in the Ministry of Justice and then transferred to the office of censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to director in the Ministry of Justice before transferring to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 當罷直，大學士阿桂素倚之，請留直如故。

translations.literal: When he was due to leave duty on the Grand Council, Grand Secretary Agui, who had long relied on him, requested that he remain on duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his term on the Grand Council was ending, Grand Secretary Agui, who had long depended on him, asked that he remain on duty without interruption.

sentences.zh: 阿桂屢奉使出剿匪、治河、閱海塘、讞獄，熊光輒從。

translations.literal: Whenever Agui was repeatedly dispatched on missions to suppress bandits, manage the rivers, inspect the sea walls, or judge criminal cases, Xiongguang invariably accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again, whenever Agui was sent out to suppress bandits, manage river works, inspect sea walls, or adjudicate cases, Xiongguang went with him.

sentences.zh: 累遷通政司參議。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted by stages to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，高宗幸熱河，夜宣軍機大臣，未至，命召章​​京，熊光入對稱旨，欲擢任軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing the Gaozong Emperor went to Rehe; at night he summoned the Grand Council ministers, but they had not arrived, so he ordered a clerk summoned. Xiongguang entered audience, pleased him, and the emperor wished to promote him to Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiaqing reign, the Gaozong Emperor traveled to Rehe. One night he summoned the Grand Council ministers, but before they arrived he called for a clerk instead. Xiongguang entered audience and satisfied the emperor, who wished to elevate him to the council.

sentences.zh: 和珅稱熊光官五品，不符體制，因薦學士戴衢亨，官四品，在軍機久，用熊光不如用衢亨，詔同加三品卿銜入直。

translations.literal: Heshen said Xiongguang was only a fifth-rank official and did not conform to regulations, so he recommended Bachelor Dai Quheng, a fourth-rank official who had long served on the Grand Council, arguing that Quheng was preferable to Xiongguang. An edict ordered both to receive the honorary third-rank grand secretary title and enter duty.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen objected that Xiongguang was only fifth rank and therefore irregular for the post, and recommended instead Bachelor Dai Quheng, fourth rank and a long-serving council clerk, as the better choice. Both men were then granted an honorary third-rank grand secretary title and admitted to council duty.

sentences.zh: 居政府六閱月，和珅忌之，出為直隸布政使。

translations.literal: After six months in the central administration, Heshen envied him and he was transferred out to be provincial treasurer of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After six months at court, Heshen grew jealous of him, and he was sent out as provincial treasurer of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 四年，高宗崩，仁宗親政，和珅伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died, the Renzong Emperor took personal rule, and Heshen was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; the Renzong Emperor assumed personal rule, and Heshen was executed.

sentences.zh: 熊光言和珅管理各部日久，多變舊章以營私，大憝雖除，猾吏仍可因緣為奸，亟宜更正，上韙之。

translations.literal: Xiongguang said Heshen had managed the various ministries for many years and had changed old regulations in many cases to serve private ends; though the great villain had been removed, crafty clerks could still exploit loopholes to practice fraud, and corrections were urgently needed. The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang argued that Heshen, after years overseeing the ministries, had altered many old rules for private gain; though the arch-criminal was gone, shrewd clerks could still abuse the system, and urgent reform was needed. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 擢河南巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 教匪逼境，熊光駐防盧氏，張漢潮竄商州，分掠藍田，疏請截留山東兵赴明亮軍協剿；

translations.literal: When the sect rebels pressed the border, Xiongguang stationed himself on defense at Lushi. Zhang Hanchao fled to Shangzhou and sent detachments to plunder Lantian. In a memorial he requested that Shandong troops be detained and sent to Ming Liang's army to assist in suppression;
translations.idiomatic: As sect rebels threatened the border, Xiongguang took up defense at Lushi. Zhang Hanchao fled toward Shangzhou and sent raiders into Lantian. Xiongguang memorialized to detain Shandong troops and attach them to Ming Liang's command for joint suppression;

sentences.zh: 復以張天倫竄近鄖陽江岸，謀犯豫南，調直隸正定標兵備剿。

translations.literal: He also, because Zhang Tianlun had fled near the Yunyang riverbank and planned to invade southern Henan, transferred regular troops from Zhengding in Zhili to prepare for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Tianlun was lurking near the Yunyang riverbank with designs on southern Henan, he also shifted regular troops from Zhengding in Zhili into readiness.

sentences.zh: 上以所見與合，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: The emperor considered his views consistent and issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found his assessments sound and issued a commendation.

sentences.zh: 尋漢潮趨雒南，遣總兵張文奇、田永桐擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon Hanchao pressed toward Luonan; he dispatched generals Zhang Wenqi and Tian Yongtong, who drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hanchao pressed toward Luonan; Xiongguang sent Generals Zhang Wenqi and Tian Yongtong, who drove him off.

sentences.zh: 令南汝光道陳鍾琛扼襄河要隘，糧道完顏岱率滿營兵協防，撥壽春鎮兵五百駐樊城。

translations.literal: He ordered Intendant Chen Zhongchen of Nan-Ru-Guang Circuit to hold the strategic passes of the Xiang River, Commissary Officer Wanyan Dai to lead Manchu garrison troops in joint defense, and detached five hundred troops from Shouchun Garrison to station at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Circuit Intendant Chen Zhongchen to hold the Xiang River's critical crossings, had Commissary Officer Wanyan Dai bring Manchu garrison troops into joint defense, and posted five hundred men from Shouchun Garrison at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 請召募練兵五千，並以開封練勇千名改為撫標新兵，從之。

translations.literal: He requested recruiting five thousand drilled soldiers and converting one thousand drilled braves at Kaifeng into new provincial-guard troops; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recruit five thousand drilled troops and convert a thousand Kaifeng militia into new provincial-guard soldiers; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，楚匪自均州、鄖縣窺渡襄河，賴預防擊退。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chu bandits from Junzhou and Yun County attempted to cross the Xiang River and were repelled thanks to prior defensive measures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, rebels from Junzhou and Yun County tried to cross the Xiang River but were beaten back by the defenses he had put in place.

sentences.zh: 上念河南兵單，命直隸、山西遣兵赴援，又命添募鄉勇，熊光疏言：「河南盧、淅一帶，原有鄉勇萬餘，而賊竄自如。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that Henan had few troops, ordered Zhili and Shanxi to dispatch reinforcements and also ordered additional recruitment of local braves. Xiongguang memorialized: "In the Luxi and Xichuan region of Henan there were originally more than ten thousand local braves, yet the bandits still roamed freely.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that Henan was understrength, the emperor ordered reinforcements from Zhili and Shanxi and further recruitment of local braves. Xiongguang replied in a memorial: "The Luxi and Xichuan region already had more than ten thousand local braves, yet rebels still moved freely there.

sentences.zh: 凡遊民應募，賊至先逃，反搖兵心。

translations.literal: Whenever idle men were enlisted, they fled first when bandits arrived, undermining the army's morale.
translations.idiomatic: Drifters enlisted as braves tended to bolt at the first sign of rebels, which only unsettled regular troops.

sentences.zh: 是以上年撤勇添兵，賊未敢肆，此兵勝於勇之明驗。

translations.literal: Therefore last year, when braves were withdrawn and regular troops added, the bandits did not dare act freely—clear proof that soldiers surpass braves.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's policy of disbanding braves and adding regulars kept the rebels in check—plain proof that soldiers outmatch militia.

sentences.zh: 今有直隸等省官兵，擇要駐守，已足策應，無庸募勇。

translations.literal: Now that troops from Zhili and other provinces are stationed at key points, that is sufficient for support; there is no need to recruit braves.
translations.idiomatic: With troops from Zhili and other provinces already posted at critical points, coordination is adequate and further militia recruitment is unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 」七月，殲寶豐、郟縣潰匪於彭山，教首劉之協遁葉縣就擒，予議敘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he destroyed routed bandits from Baofeng and Jia County at Pengshan; the sect leader Liu Zhixie, who had fled to Ye County, was captured, and rewards were proposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he annihilated routed rebels from Baofeng and Jia County at Pengshan. Sect leader Liu Zhixie, who had fled to Ye County, was captured, and merit rewards were proposed.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 途遇協防陝西兵二百餘人，逃回本營，廉得其缺餉狀，杖首謀者二人，餘釋不問。

translations.literal: On the road he encountered more than two hundred Shaanxi troops assigned to joint defense who had deserted back to their camp; he investigated and found they lacked rations and pay, caned the two ringleaders, and released the rest without further punishment.
translations.idiomatic: En route he met more than two hundred Shaanxi troops on joint-defense duty who had deserted to their own camp. Finding they had gone unpaid, he flogged the two ringleaders and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 房縣鄉勇糾搶民寨，縛送三十餘人，立誅之。

translations.literal: Local braves in Fang County had banded together to raid civilian stockades; he had more than thirty bound and sent in, and had them executed forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: Militia in Fang County had banded together to loot civilian stockades; he had more than thirty of them bound and brought in, then executed them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 提督長齡、巡撫全保率師防剿，迭敗湯思蛟、劉朝選等。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Chang Ling and Governor Quan Bao led armies in defense and suppression and repeatedly defeated Tang Sijiao, Liu Chaoxuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Chang Ling and Governor Quan Bao led defensive and punitive operations and repeatedly defeated Tang Sijiao, Liu Chaoxuan, and others.

sentences.zh: 川匪擾興山、竹谿、房縣，分兵追剿，殲獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Sichuan bandits harassed Xingshan, Zhuxi, and Fang County; he divided his forces in pursuit and suppression and killed or captured a great number.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan rebels harassed Xingshan, Zhuxi, and Fang County; he split his forces in pursuit and killed or captured large numbers.

sentences.zh: 平樊人傑餘匪，俘賊首崔宗和。

translations.literal: He pacified the remnant bandits of Fan Renjie and captured the bandit chief Cui Zonghe.
translations.idiomatic: He mopped up Fan Renjie's remaining followers and captured rebel chief Cui Zonghe.

sentences.zh: 上以熊光調度供支，迭詔褒獎。

translations.literal: Because of Xiongguang's command arrangements and supplies, the emperor repeatedly issued edicts of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly commended him for his logistical command and provisioning.

sentences.zh: 新設湖北提督，改移鄖陽鎮協，添兵三千五百名，即以無業鄉勇充之。

translations.literal: A new regional commander post was created for Hubei; the Yunyang garrison command was reorganized with an additional three thousand five hundred troops, to be filled by unemployed local braves.
translations.idiomatic: A new Hubei regional command was established, the Yunyang garrison was reorganized, and three thousand five hundred additional troops were raised from unemployed local militia.

sentences.zh: 又奏定稽查寨勇章程，略言：「寨勇習於戰鬥，輕視官兵，流弊不可不慮。

translations.literal: He also memorialized fixed regulations for inspecting stockade braves, stating in brief: "Stockade braves are accustomed to fighting and look down on regular troops; the abuses this invites cannot be ignored.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted regulations for auditing stockade militia, noting: "Stockade braves are practiced in combat and hold regular troops in contempt; the abuses that follow cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 今將寨堡戶口、器械逐一登記，陽資其力以助此日之軍威，默挈其綱以弭將來之民患。

translations.literal: Now the households and weapons of every stockade and fort will be registered one by one—openly drawing on their strength to bolster the army's authority today, while quietly holding their leash to forestall future harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Every stockade's households and arms would be registered—openly enlisting their strength for present military needs while quietly keeping control to prevent future abuses against civilians.

sentences.zh: 」上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，三省匪平，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the bandits of the three provinces were pacified, and he was granted the honorary title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, with the three provinces pacified, he received the honorary title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遣撤鄉勇，以叛產變價給賞，詔嘉其撙節。

translations.literal: He dismissed local braves and used proceeds from the sale of rebel property to pay rewards; an edict praised his thrift.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded local militia and paid rewards from the sale of confiscated rebel property; the court praised his economy.

sentences.zh: 九年，劾湖南巡撫高杞違例調補知縣，杞坐降調。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he impeached Hunan Governor Gao Qi for irregular transfer and appointment of magistrates; Qi was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he impeached Hunan Governor Gao Qi for illegally transferring and appointing magistrates; Qi was demoted and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，侍郎初彭齡劾熊光受沔陽知州秦泰金，及兩淮匣費，上詰彭齡，以得自高杞對。

translations.literal: Before long, Vice Minister Chu Pengling impeached Xiongguang for accepting gifts from Qianyang Prefect Qin Taijin and for the treasury-box fees of the Two Huai, the emperor questioned Pengling, who answered that he had learned this from Gao Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Vice Minister Chu Pengling accused Xiongguang of accepting gifts from Qianyang Prefect Qin Taijin and of mishandling Two Huai treasury-box fees. When the emperor questioned Pengling, he said the charges came from Gao Qi.

sentences.zh: 命巡撫全保按驗無跡，彭齡、杞俱獲譴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Governor Quan Bao to investigate; no evidence was found, and both Pengling and Qi were censured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Governor Quan Bao to investigate; no evidence emerged, and both Pengling and Qi were punished.

sentences.zh: 傳諭熊光返躬自省，平心辦事，戒勿躁妄。

translations.literal: An edict was sent instructing Xiongguang to examine himself, handle affairs even-handedly, and guard against rashness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang was told to look inward, keep his judgment even, and avoid rashness.

sentences.zh: 十年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣總督那彥成與湖廣總督百齡互訐，命偕侍郎托津赴湖北按之。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Nayancheng of the Two Guang and Governor-General Bailing of Huguang were mutually impeaching each other; the emperor ordered Xiongguang together with Vice Minister Tuojin to go to Hubei to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Governor-General Nayancheng of the Two Guang and Governor-General Bailing of Huguang were trading accusations; Xiongguang was sent with Vice Minister Tuojin to Hubei to investigate.

sentences.zh: 百齡被訐，事有跡。

translations.literal: Bailing was impeached and there were traces of wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: The charges against Bailing proved partly substantiated.

sentences.zh: 方鞫治，未定讞，那彥成亦以倡撫洋盜逮京，調熊光兩廣總督。

translations.literal: While the case was being tried but before judgment was fixed, Nayancheng was also arrested and brought to the capital for advocating appeasement of foreign pirates, and Xiongguang was transferred to be governor-general of the Two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: While the inquiry was still underway, Nayancheng was also arrested in the capital for advocating leniency toward foreign pirates, and Xiongguang was transferred to govern the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 會直隸官吏勾通侵帑事發，歷任總督籓司俱獲譴。

translations.literal: Meanwhile a case of collusion and embezzlement by Zhili officials came to light, and successive governors-general and treasurers were all censured.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a Zhili embezzlement ring came to light, and successive governors-general and treasurers were censured.

sentences.zh: 上以熊光任籓司無虛收，任總督無失察，特詔嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor noted that during Xiongguang's service as treasurer he had taken no illicit receipts and as governor-general had not failed in oversight, and specially issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that as treasurer Xiongguang had taken no illicit receipts and as governor-general had not failed in oversight, and issued a special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，英吉利兵船十三艘泊香山雞頸洋，其酋率兵三百擅入澳門，佔踞砲台，兵艦駛進黃埔。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, thirteen English warships anchored at Jijing Bay off Xiangshan; their chief led three hundred men in unauthorized entry into Macau, seized the batteries, and the warships sailed into Whampoa.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, thirteen British warships anchored at Jijing Bay off Xiangshan. Their commander led three hundred men in an unauthorized entry into Macau, seized the batteries, and the fleet pressed into Whampoa.

sentences.zh: 熊光以英人志在貿易，其兵費出於商稅，惟封關足以制其死命；

translations.literal: Xiongguang held that the English aimed at trade, that their military expenses came from commercial taxes, and that only closing the port could hold their vital interests in check;
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang argued that the British wanted trade, that their military costs depended on commercial taxes, and that closing the port was the surest way to bring them to heel;

sentences.zh: 若輕率用兵，彼船砲勝我數倍，戰必不敵，而東南沿海將受其害，意主持重。

translations.literal: if troops were rashly committed, their ships and guns exceeded China's several times over and battle would surely be lost, while the southeast coast would suffer harm—his view was to hold a cautious line.
translations.idiomatic: but that rash military action would invite defeat against a fleet whose guns far outmatched China's and would expose the southeast coast to harm. He favored restraint.

sentences.zh: 踰月始上聞，言已令停止開艙，俟退出澳門，方准貿易。

translations.literal: More than a month passed before he reported to the throne, saying he had ordered trade halted until they withdrew from Macau, after which commerce could resume.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed before he memorialized the throne, reporting that he had halted trade and would reopen it only after the British quit Macau.

sentences.zh: 上以熊光未即調兵，故示弱，嚴詔切責。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that because Xiongguang had not immediately mobilized troops he had shown weakness, and issued a stern edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Xiongguang's failure to mobilize immediately had shown weakness and issued a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 洋舶遷延至十月始陸續去。

translations.literal: The foreign ships lingered until the tenth month before departing one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign vessels lingered until the tenth month before leaving in succession.

sentences.zh: 下吏議，褫職，效力南河。

translations.literal: The case was referred to the judicial officials; he was stripped of office and ordered to serve at the Southern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: After judicial review he was stripped of rank and ordered to serve on the Southern Rivers project.

sentences.zh: 百齡代其任，疏言熊光葸懦，上益怒，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Bailing replaced him in office and memorialized that Xiongguang was timid and cowardly; the emperor grew still angrier and sent him into exile at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Bailing succeeded him and memorialized that Xiongguang had been timid and irresolute; the emperor's anger deepened, and Xiongguang was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召還，授兵部主事，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War, and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was recalled, given a post as secretary in the Ministry of War, and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 道光八年，重與鹿鳴宴，加四品卿銜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang he again attended the Luming banquet and was granted the honorary fourth-rank grand secretary title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Daoguang reign he again attended the Luming banquet and received an honorary fourth-rank grand secretary title.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於家，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died at home, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died at home at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 熊光嘗曰：「刑賞者，聖主之大權，而以其柄寄於封圻大吏。

translations.literal: Xiongguang once said: "Punishment and reward are the great prerogatives of a sage ruler, yet their handle is entrusted to frontier governors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang once said: "Punishment and reward belong to the sage ruler alone, yet their power is delegated to frontier governors.

sentences.zh: 若以有司援案比例，求免駁斥之術處之，舛矣。

translations.literal: If one handles them by having subordinate officials cite precedents and proportions to avoid rejection, that is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: To handle them by having subordinates cite precedents merely to avoid rejection is a mistake.

sentences.zh: 刑一人，賞一人，而有益於世道人心，雖不符於例，所必及也。

translations.literal: To punish one person or reward one person when it benefits public morals and the hearts of the people, even if it does not conform to precedent, one must still do it.
translations.idiomatic: If punishing or rewarding someone will benefit public morals and the people's hearts, one must act even when precedent does not fit.

sentences.zh: 不得請，必再三爭，乃為不負。

translations.literal: If permission is not granted, one must argue again and again—only then has one fulfilled one's duty.
translations.idiomatic: If the court refuses, one must argue repeatedly—only then has one done one's duty.

sentences.zh: 若憂嫌畏譏，隨波逐流，其咎不止溺職而已。

translations.literal: If one worries about suspicion and fears ridicule and drifts with the current, the fault is more than mere dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: To fret over suspicion, fear ridicule, and drift with the tide is a fault worse than simple dereliction.

sentences.zh: 」當調直隸，入覲，上曰：「教匪淨盡，天下自此太平。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Zhili and entered audience, the emperor said: "The sect rebels are wholly eliminated; the realm will henceforth be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Zhili and received audience, the emperor said: "The sect rebels are wholly eliminated; the realm will be at peace from now on.

sentences.zh: 」熊光曰：「督撫率郡縣加意撫循，提鎮率將弁加意訓練，百姓有恩可懷，有威可畏，太平自不難致。

translations.literal: Xiongguang said: "If governors and governors-general lead the prefectures and counties in attentive care and consolation, and regional commanders and garrison commanders lead the officers in attentive training, so that the people have kindness to cherish and authority to fear, peace will not be hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang replied: "If governors lead their prefectures and counties in attentive care, and regional commanders train their officers diligently, so that the people feel both kindness and awe, peace will not be hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 若稍懈，則伏戎於莽，吳起所謂舟中皆敵國也。

translations.literal: If one slackens even slightly, enemies lie hidden in the thickets—what Wu Qi called having every seat in the boat an enemy state.
translations.idiomatic: But slacken even slightly, and enemies lie hidden in the thickets—as Wu Qi said, every seat in the boat becomes an enemy state.

sentences.zh: 」及東巡返，迎駕夷齊廟，與董誥、戴衢亨同對。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from an eastern tour, Xiongguang met the imperial procession at the Yi-Qi Temple and entered audience together with Dong Gao and Dai Quheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from an eastern tour, Xiongguang met the imperial procession at the Yi-Qi Temple and entered audience with Dong Gao and Dai Quheng.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「道路風景甚佳！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The scenery along the road is excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The scenery along the road is splendid!

sentences.zh: 」熊光越次言曰：「皇上此行，欲稽祖宗創業艱難之跡，為萬世子孫法，風景何足言耶？

translations.literal: Xiongguang spoke out of turn: "Your Majesty's journey aims to examine the traces of the ancestral founders' arduous enterprise and set an example for ten thousand generations of descendants—what is scenery worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang spoke out of turn: "Your Majesty's journey is meant to trace the hardships of the founding ancestors and set an example for generations to come—what is scenery beside that?

sentences.zh: 」上有頃又曰：「汝蘇州人，朕少扈蹕過之，其風景誠無匹。

translations.literal: After a moment the emperor said again: "You are a Suzhou man; I once followed the imperial procession there in my youth, and its scenery truly has no equal.
translations.idiomatic: After a pause the emperor added: "You are from Suzhou; I passed through there in my youth on imperial progress, and its scenery truly has no equal.

sentences.zh: 」熊光曰：「皇上所見，乃剪採為花。

translations.literal: Xiongguang said: "What Your Majesty saw was flowers cut and arranged for display.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang said: "What Your Majesty saw was flowers cut and arranged for show.

sentences.zh: 蘇州惟虎丘稱名勝，實一墳堆之大者！

translations.literal: In Suzhou only Tiger Hill is called a famous scenic spot, and in truth it is merely a large mound!
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou only Tiger Hill counts as a famous sight, and in truth it is little more than a large burial mound!

sentences.zh: 城中河道逼仄，糞船擁擠，何足言風景？

translations.literal: The city canals are narrow and cramped, and night-soil boats crowd them—what is there to call scenery?
translations.idiomatic: The city canals are cramped and crowded with night-soil boats—what scenery is there to speak of?

sentences.zh: 」上又曰：「如汝言，皇考何為六度至彼？

translations.literal: The emperor said again: "If what you say is so, why did my late father go there six times?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again: "If that is so, why did my late father visit there six times?

sentences.zh: 」熊光叩頭曰：「皇上至孝，臣從前侍皇上謁太上皇帝，蒙諭『朕臨御六十年，並無失德。

translations.literal: Xiongguang kowtowed and said: "Your Majesty is supremely filial. When I formerly attended Your Majesty in audience with the Retired Emperor, I received his instruction: 'I have ruled for sixty years without any lapse in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongguang kowtowed and said: "Your Majesty is supremely filial. When I once attended Your Majesty in audience with the Retired Emperor, he told us: 'I have ruled for sixty years without any lapse in virtue.

sentences.zh: 惟六次南巡，勞民傷財，作無益害有益。

translations.literal: Only the six southern tours exhausted the people and wasted resources, doing what was useless and harming what was useful.
translations.idiomatic: Only the six southern tours exhausted the people and wasted resources, doing harm where there should have been benefit.

sentences.zh: 將來皇帝如南巡，而汝不阻止，必無以對朕』。

translations.literal: If a future emperor makes a southern tour and you do not stop him, you will have no way to answer to me.'
translations.idiomatic: If a future emperor makes a southern tour and you do not stop him, you will have no way to answer to me.'

sentences.zh: 仁聖之所悔，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: What the benevolent sage regretted still rings in the ears.
translations.idiomatic: What that benevolent sage regretted still rings in the ears.

sentences.zh: 」同列皆震悚，壯其敢言。

translations.literal: His colleagues were all shaken and awed, and admired his boldness in speaking.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were shaken, yet admired his boldness.

sentences.zh: 後熊光告人，「墳堆」、「糞船」兩語，乃乾隆初故相訥親奏疏所言，重述之耳。

translations.literal: Later Xiongguang told others that the two phrases "burial mound" and "night-soil boat" were what the former chief minister Neqin had said in a memorial at the beginning of the Qianlong reign—he had merely repeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiongguang told others that the phrases "burial mound" and "night-soil boat" came from a memorial by the former chief minister Neqin at the start of the Qianlong reign—he had only repeated them.

sentences.zh: 熊光晚年著伊江別錄、春明補錄、葑溪筆錄三書，紀所聞名臣言行，多可法雲。

translations.literal: In his later years Xiongguang wrote three books—Records from Yijiang, Supplementary Records from Chunming, and Notes from Fengxi—recording the words and deeds of eminent ministers he had heard of, many of them worthy of emulation.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Xiongguang wrote three books—Records from Yijiang, Supplementary Records from Chunming, and Notes from Fengxi—recording the words and deeds of eminent ministers he had known, many worthy of emulation.

sentences.zh: 汪志伊，字稼門，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiyi, style name Jiamen, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyi, styled Jiamen, was from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年舉人，充四庫館校對，議敘，授山西靈石知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate, served as a proofreader in the Siku Library project, received merit appointment, and was appointed magistrate of Lingshi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign, he served as a proofreader on the Siku Library project, received merit appointment, and became magistrate of Lingshi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 除徵糧擾累，刻木為皁隸書里分糧數，以次傳遞，民遵輸納。

translations.literal: He eliminated the harassment involved in grain collection, carved wooden tallies on which runners recorded each hamlet's grain quota, passed them in sequence, and the people complied in paying.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the harassment of grain collection by carving wooden tallies on which runners recorded each hamlet's quota in sequence, and the people paid without dispute.

sentences.zh: 調榆次，遷霍州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yuci and promoted to prefect of Huozhou Direct Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yuci and promoted to prefect of Huozhou Direct Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代州民孟木成殺人，已定讞情實，其弟代呼冤，巡撫勒保檄志伊往按，平反之。

translations.literal: A man of Daizhou, Meng Mucheng, had killed someone; the case was judged substantiated, but his younger brother pleaded his innocence on his behalf. Governor Lebao ordered Zhiyi to investigate, and he reversed the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Mucheng of Daizhou was convicted of murder, his younger brother pleaded his innocence. Governor Lebao ordered Zhiyi to reinvestigate, and he reversed the verdict.

sentences.zh: 承審者護前失，不決，命大臣臨鞫，重違眾議，志伊堅執與爭，孟木成竟得免死。

translations.literal: The original judges defended their earlier error and would not decide; a high minister was ordered to preside at trial. Though this went against the majority view, Zhiyi held firm and argued, and Meng Mucheng was ultimately spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The original judges clung to their earlier error and would not decide, so a senior minister was sent to preside. Though Zhiyi stood against the majority, he held firm, and Meng Mucheng was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 志伊以此負強項名。

translations.literal: Because of this Zhiyi acquired a reputation for stubbornness.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gained a reputation for stubborn integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢江蘇鎮江知府，調蘇州，連擢蘇松糧道、按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu, transferred to Suzhou, and promoted in succession to grain intendant of Su-Song and provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu, transferred to Suzhou, and rose in succession to grain intendant of Su-Song and provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，遷甘肅布政使，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Gansu and then moved to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he became provincial treasurer of Gansu and was then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 江、浙漕重積弊，由官吏規費多。

translations.literal: The grain transport systems of Jiangsu and Zhejiang had deep accumulated abuses, arising from the many customary fees taken by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu and Zhejiang grain transport suffered deep abuses rooted in the many customary fees officials collected.

sentences.zh: 志伊曆任，皆先除規費之在官者，然後以次裁革，嚴設科條。

translations.literal: In every post Zhiyi held, he first eliminated the customary fees taken by officials, then cut them away step by step and established strict regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held, Zhiyi first eliminated official customary fees, then cut the rest away step by step and imposed strict regulations.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，以杭州、乍浦駐防營養贍錢三月未放，被劾，議降二級調用，詔以志伊平日操守尚好，加恩授江西按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, because stipends for the garrison camps at Hangzhou and Zhapu had gone unpaid for three months, he was impeached and demotion by two ranks and transfer were proposed; an edict noted that Zhiyi's conduct had ordinarily been good and granted him clemency with appointment as provincial judge of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign, he was impeached because garrison stipends at Hangzhou and Zhapu had gone unpaid for three months. Demotion by two ranks was proposed, but the court noted his ordinarily good conduct and appointed him provincial judge of Jiangxi as a grace.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷福建布政使，未數月，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Fujian, and within a few months was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became provincial treasurer of Fujian and, within a few months, was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 時海盜方張，仁宗於閩事特加意。

translations.literal: At that time pirates were on the rise, and the Renzong Emperor paid special attention to affairs in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates were then on the rise, and the Renzong Emperor paid special attention to Fujian affairs.

sentences.zh: 志伊屢疏陳水師人材難得，請寬疏防處分，變通選補章程，副參以上，兼用本省之人；

translations.literal: Zhiyi repeatedly memorialized that talented naval officers were hard to find, requested leniency in penalties for lapses in coastal defense, and proposed flexible selection and appointment regulations: for deputy commanders and above, men from the same province should be used together with others;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi repeatedly memorialized that capable naval officers were hard to find, asked leniency for lapses in coastal defense, and proposed flexible appointment rules: for deputy commanders and above, men from the same province should be used alongside others;

sentences.zh: 以下，兩省通融撥用。

translations.literal: below that rank, the two provinces should exchange and assign personnel flexibly.
translations.idiomatic: below that rank, the two provinces should exchange personnel flexibly.

sentences.zh: 又州縣徵糧處分過嚴，升調要缺難得合例，請人地相需者，不拘俸滿參罰。

translations.literal: He also noted that penalties for grain collection at the prefecture and county level were too severe, making it hard to find qualified candidates for key vacancies on promotion and transfer, and requested that where men and posts matched need, terms of service and prior penalties need not be strictly applied.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that penalties for grain collection were too harsh to fill key vacancies on promotion, and asked that where a man fit a post, service terms and prior penalties be waived.

sentences.zh: 皆允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 詔飭嚴懲會匪及械鬥惡習。

translations.literal: An edict ordered strict punishment of secret-society bandits and the evil custom of armed feuding.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered harsh punishment of secret-society bandits and the custom of armed feuding.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏報漳、泉一帶，匪徒節經剿捕，均知斂跡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized that in the Zhangzhou and Quanzhou region, bandits had been repeatedly suppressed and captured and had all learned to restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he reported that bandits in the Zhangzhou and Quanzhou region, after repeated suppression, had learned to keep quiet.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「滋事不法，有犯必懲，不可無事滋擾。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Those who cause trouble and break the law must be punished when they offend; one must not harass people when there is no cause.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Lawbreakers who cause trouble must be punished, but officials must not harass the innocent.

sentences.zh: 責以鎮靜，不可姑息養奸，亦不可持之太蹙。

translations.literal: They are charged to keep calm, neither indulging evil nor pressing too hard.
translations.idiomatic: Keep calm: neither indulge wrongdoers nor press too hard.

sentences.zh: 」尋奏龍溪、詔安、馬港、海澄四廳縣，遴員治理，民不械鬥。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized that in the four subprefectures and counties of Longxi, Zhao'an, Magang, and Haicheng, selected officials had been appointed to govern, and the people no longer engaged in armed feuds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he reported that in Longxi, Zhao'an, Magang, and Haicheng, carefully chosen officials had ended armed feuding among the people.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「一經良有司整飭，改除積習，是小民不難化導，要在親民之官得人。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Once good officials have put things in order and removed deep-rooted customs, ordinary people are not hard to guide and transform—the key is that officials close to the people must be the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Once capable officials put things in order and broke old habits, ordinary people proved easy to guide—the key is appointing the right men close to the people.

sentences.zh: 當於平日遴選賢員，俾實心任事，為正本清源之道。

translations.literal: In ordinary times one should select worthy officials and let them serve in earnest—that is the way to cure the root and clear the source.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy officials should be chosen in ordinary times and allowed to serve wholeheartedly—that is the way to cure problems at the root.

sentences.zh: 」志伊薦閩縣知縣王紹蘭，上素知其人，詔嘉志伊能留心察吏。

translations.literal: Zhiyi recommended Min County Magistrate Wang Shaolan; the emperor already knew the man and issued an edict praising Zhiyi for paying attention to evaluating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi recommended Min County Magistrate Wang Shaolan. The emperor already knew Wang and praised Zhiyi for keeping a close eye on officials.

sentences.zh: 既而偕總督玉德，疏請泉州知府錢學彬改京職，上斥疏語矛盾。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Governor-General Yude, he memorialized requesting that Quanzhou Prefect Qian Xuebin be transferred to a capital post; the emperor rebuked the memorial's contradictory language.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and Governor-General Yude memorialized to transfer Quanzhou Prefect Qian Xuebin to a capital post; the emperor rebuked the memorial as contradictory.

sentences.zh: 尋究得學彬任聽家人舞弊婪贓事，坐察吏不明，議革任，特寬之。

translations.literal: An investigation soon found that Xuebin had allowed his household to practice fraud and extort bribes; he was judged for failing to supervise officials clearly, dismissal was proposed, but he was specially granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation soon showed Xuebin had let his household commit fraud and extort bribes. He was judged for poor oversight and dismissal was proposed, but the court showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 六年，病，請解職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he fell ill and requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he fell ill and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 八年，起署副都御史、刑部侍郎，授江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled to serve as acting vice censor-in-chief and vice minister of justice, then appointed governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as acting vice censor-in-chief and vice minister of justice, then appointed governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 給事中蕭芝請就產米之鄉採買，由海運京，下議，志伊言其不便，罷之。

translations.literal: Censorate drafter Xiao Zhi proposed purchasing grain in rice-producing districts and shipping it to the capital by sea; the matter was referred for discussion, Zhiyi said it was impractical, and it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate drafter Xiao Zhi proposed buying grain in rice-producing districts and shipping it to the capital by sea. After discussion Zhiyi argued it was impractical, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 九年，清江浦淤淺，糧船停滯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Qingjiangpu channel silted up and grain transports stalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Qingjiangpu channel silted up and grain transports stalled.

sentences.zh: 上慮京倉缺米，詔志伊預籌，請碾常平倉穀三千石備撥。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing a shortage in the capital granaries, ordered Zhiyi to plan ahead; he requested milling three thousand shi of grain from the Ever-Normal Granaries for reserve allocation.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a shortage in the capital granaries, the emperor ordered Zhiyi to plan ahead; he asked to mill three thousand shi from the Ever-Normal Granaries as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 以新漕減運，命酌量採買，志伊疏言：「安徽民田有一歲兩收者，各令七月完納漕糧，九十月可運通。

translations.literal: Because the new tribute grain transport was reduced, the emperor ordered discretionary purchase; Zhiyi memorialized: "In Anhui some civilian fields yield two harvests a year; if each were required to complete tribute grain payment in the seventh month, transport to the capital could be completed in the ninth and tenth months.
translations.idiomatic: With new tribute transport reduced, the emperor ordered discretionary grain purchases. Zhiyi memorialized: "In Anhui some fields yield two harvests a year; if tribute were paid in the seventh month, grain could reach the capital by the ninth and tenth months.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣亦如之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Huguang could do the same.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi and Huguang could follow the same schedule.

sentences.zh: 」上以一歲兩徵近加賦，且來歲仍屬短絀，斥為迂繆。

translations.literal: The emperor, noting that double collection in one year resembled an added levy and that the next year would still fall short, dismissed the proposal as impractical and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed the idea as impractical, noting that collecting twice in one year amounted to an added levy and that shortages would persist the next year.

sentences.zh: 尋奏採米十二萬石搭運，報聞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized purchasing one hundred twenty thousand shi of grain for supplementary transport and reported completion.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported purchasing one hundred twenty thousand shi for supplementary transport.

sentences.zh: 時江北淮、揚水災，徐、海苦旱。

translations.literal: At that time north of the Yangzi the Huai and Yang regions suffered flood, while Xuzhou and Haizhou endured drought.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yangzi the Huai and Yang regions flooded while Xuzhou and Haizhou suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 志伊手編荒政輯要，頒屬吏為賑濟之法。

translations.literal: Zhiyi personally compiled Essentials of Famine Administration and distributed it to subordinate officials as a method for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi compiled Essentials of Famine Administration and distributed it to subordinates as a guide for relief work.

sentences.zh: 蘇州人文薈萃，增設正誼書院課士。

translations.literal: Suzhou was rich in scholars; he added the Zhengyi Academy to instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou was rich in scholars, and he established the Zhengyi Academy to instruct students.

sentences.zh: 奏請頒御製詩文集於江南各書院，上勿許，曰：「朕之政治即文章，何必以文字炫長耶？

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting distribution of the emperor's collected poems and essays to academies throughout Jiangnan; the emperor refused, saying: "My governance itself is literature—why must I display my literary prowess?
translations.idiomatic: He asked to distribute the emperor's collected poems and essays to Jiangnan academies. The emperor refused: "My governance is my literature—why display literary prowess?

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 川、楚餘匪散匿洞庭湖，環湖數府州多盜。

translations.literal: Remnant bandits from Sichuan and Huguang scattered and hid around Dongting Lake, and the prefectures and departments circling the lake had many robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant bandits from Sichuan and Huguang hid around Dongting Lake, and the surrounding prefectures were rife with robbers.

sentences.zh: 志伊多選幹吏偵訪，檄下分捕，盜無所匿。

translations.literal: Zhiyi selected many capable officials for investigation, issued orders for separate capture, and the robbers had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi sent capable officials to investigate, ordered separate captures, and robbers had nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 濱江地自乾隆末大水湮沒，民田未復。

translations.literal: Riverside land had been submerged in the great flood at the end of the Qianlong reign, and civilian fields had not been restored.
translations.idiomatic: Riverside land submerged in the great flood at the end of the Qianlong reign had not been restored to cultivation.

sentences.zh: 親駕小舟，歷勘疏塞，建二閘於第江口、福田寺，以時啟閉。

translations.literal: He personally took a small boat to survey and dredge blockages, built two sluice gates at Dijiangkou and Futian Temple, and opened and closed them according to season.
translations.idiomatic: He personally surveyed blockages by small boat, built sluice gates at Dijiangkou and Futian Temple, and operated them on schedule.

sentences.zh: 十六年，調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先是湖北應山民喻春謀殺人，其母以刑求誣服，控於京，命志伊提鞫。

translations.literal: Earlier a man of Yingshan in Hubei, Yu Chun, had been accused of plotting murder; his mother had been forced by torture into a false confession, appealed to the capital, and the emperor ordered Zhiyi to conduct the trial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Chun of Yingshan in Hubei had been accused of plotting murder. His mother had been tortured into a false confession and appealed to the capital; the emperor ordered Zhiyi to retry the case.

sentences.zh: 同知劉曜唐等誘供翻案，以無辜之葉秀承兇，而無左證。

translations.literal: Subprefect Liu Yaotang and others induced confessions to reverse the case, making the innocent Ye Xiu bear the guilt of the murder, yet there was no corroborating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefect Liu Yaotang and others induced confessions to reverse the verdict, making the innocent Ye Xiu bear the murder, without corroborating evidence.

sentences.zh: 巡撫同興為之平反，奏劾。

translations.literal: Governor Tongxing reversed the verdict on their behalf and memorialized to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tongxing reversed the verdict and impeached those involved.

sentences.zh: 至是入覲召對，為劉曜唐等剖辯，原代認處分。

translations.literal: When he now entered audience, he argued on behalf of Liu Yaotang and the others and offered to accept punishment in their place.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he argued on behalf of Liu Yaotang and the others and offered to accept their punishment himself.

sentences.zh: 上斥其偏執，嚴議革職，改留任。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked his obstinacy, proposed strict dismissal from office, but changed it to retention in post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his obstinacy, proposed dismissal, but allowed him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 捕誅海盜黃治，其黨吳屬乞降。

translations.literal: He captured and executed the pirate Huang Zhi; his follower Wu Shu begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed pirate Huang Zhi; follower Wu Shu begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時降盜多授官，志伊曰：「是獎盜也！

translations.literal: At that time surrendered pirates were often given official posts; Zhiyi said: "That is rewarding piracy!
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered pirates were then often given official posts. Zhiyi said: "That rewards piracy!

sentences.zh: 」仍依律遣戍。

translations.literal: He still sent them into exile according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He still sent Wu into exile according to law.

sentences.zh: 舊有天地等會匪熊毛者，創立仁義會，授張顯魯傳煽。

translations.literal: Formerly there was a Tiandihui bandit named Xiong Mao who founded the Renyi Society and appointed Zhang Xianlu to spread and incite it.
translations.idiomatic: A Tiandihui bandit named Xiong Mao had founded the Renyi Society and appointed Zhang Xianlu to spread its influence.

sentences.zh: 事覺，顯魯伏誅，毛遁，募寧化生員李玉衡捕殺之，奏賜玉衡舉人。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Xianlu was executed; Mao fled; Zhiyi recruited the Ninghua licentiate Li Yuheng to capture and kill him, and memorialized granting Yuheng the rank of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Xianlu was executed. Mao fled, but Zhiyi recruited Ninghua licentiate Li Yuheng to capture and kill him, and recommended Yuheng for provincial graduate status.

sentences.zh: 布政使李賡芸，廉吏也，為志伊所薦舉至監司。

translations.literal: Provincial treasurer Li Gengyun was an honest official whom Zhiyi had recommended and promoted to the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial treasurer Li Gengyun was an honest official whom Zhiyi had recommended to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會龍溪知縣硃履中以不職劾，因訐賡芸婪索，遽劾訊。

translations.literal: When Longxi Magistrate Zhu Lüzhong was impeached for incompetence, he accused Gengyun of extortion, and Zhiyi hastily impeached and interrogated Gengyun.
translations.idiomatic: When Longxi Magistrate Zhu Lüzhong was impeached for incompetence, he accused Gengyun of extortion, and Zhiyi hastily ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 履中已自承誣告，志伊固執駁詰，福州知府塗以輈迎合逼供，賡芸自經死，輿論大譁。

translations.literal: Lüzhong had already confessed to false accusation, but Zhiyi stubbornly pressed the inquiry; Fuzhou Prefect Tu Yizhou catered to him and forced confessions; Gengyun hanged himself, and public opinion erupted.
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong had already confessed to a false accusation, but Zhiyi pressed on. Fuzhou Prefect Tu Yizhou catered to him and forced confessions. Gengyun hanged himself, and public outrage erupted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命侍郎熙昌、副都御史王引之往按，得其狀，詔斥志伊衰邁謬誤，褫職永不敘用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Vice Minister Xichang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yinzhi were ordered to investigate; the facts were established, and an edict rebuked Zhiyi as aged, senile, and mistaken, stripped him of office, and barred him from future appointment forever.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Vice Minister Xichang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yinzhi investigated and confirmed the facts. An edict rebuked Zhiyi as aged and mistaken, stripped him of office, and barred him from future appointment.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 志伊矯廉好名，自峻崖岸。

translations.literal: Zhiyi affected integrity and loved reputation, holding himself aloof on a steep cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi affected integrity and loved reputation, holding himself aloof.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初甚鄉用，時論毀譽參半焉。

translations.literal: At first the Renzong Emperor greatly favored him for his native district, and contemporary opinion was evenly divided between praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor initially favored him highly, and contemporary opinion was evenly divided.

sentences.zh: 卒以偏執獲咎。

translations.literal: In the end he incurred blame for obstinacy.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he fell for obstinacy.

sentences.zh: 陳大文，河南杞縣人，原籍浙江會稽。

translations.literal: Chen Dawen was a native of Qixian in Henan, with original domicile in Kuaiji, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dawen was from Qixian in Henan, with ancestral roots in Kuaiji, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the thirty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign, he became a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 典廣東鄉試，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the Guangdong provincial examination and was promoted by stages to director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Guangdong provincial examination and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，出為廣西南寧知府，擢雲南迤東道。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he went out as prefect of Nanning in Guangxi and was promoted to intendant of Yidong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he became prefect of Nanning in Guangxi and was promoted to intendant of Yidong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 歷貴州、安徽按察使，江寧布政使，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He served as provincial judge of Guizhou and Anhui and provincial treasurer of Jiangning, winning reputation in each post.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial judge of Guizhou and Anhui and treasurer of Jiangning, he earned a strong reputation in each post.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，補廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He returned on his father's death, and after mourning was appointed provincial treasurer of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He returned on his father's death, and after mourning became provincial treasurer of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 總督硃珪薦大文操守廉潔，化其偏僻，可倚用，詔人才難得，命珪加以勸迪，俾成有用才。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhu Gui recommended Dawen as honest and incorrupt in conduct, capable of reforming his narrowness, and fit for reliance; an edict said talent was hard to find and ordered Gui to counsel and guide him so he might become useful talent.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhu Gui recommended Dawen as honest and capable of reforming his narrowness. The court said talent was hard to find and ordered Zhu to guide him into becoming a useful official.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiaqing reign he was appointed governor.

sentences.zh: 海盜方熾，大文以運鹽為名，集商船載鄉勇出洋，擊沉盜船六，斬獲二百餘人，賜花翎；

translations.literal: Pirates were then rampant; Dawen, under the pretext of salt transport, gathered merchant ships carrying local braves to sea, sank six pirate vessels, killed or captured more than two hundred men, and was granted the peacock feather;
translations.idiomatic: Pirates were rampant. Dawen, under the pretext of salt transport, gathered merchant ships with local militia, sank six pirate vessels, killed or captured more than two hundred men, and received the peacock feather;

sentences.zh: 屬縣不職者，列案劾治。

translations.literal: in subordinate counties he listed and impeached incompetent officials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: and he impeached incompetent officials in subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其捕盜察吏皆有實心，予議敘。

translations.literal: An edict praised his earnestness in both capturing pirates and supervising officials, and merit rewards were proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his earnestness in capturing pirates and supervising officials, and merit rewards were proposed.

sentences.zh: 尋兼署總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also served as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 四年，調山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 濟、曹兩府水災，興工代賑，州縣玩視者立劾；

translations.literal: The Ji and Cao prefectures suffered flood; he launched work-for-relief projects and immediately impeached prefectural and county officials who treated the matter lightly;
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji and Cao prefectures flooded, he launched work-for-relief projects and immediately impeached officials who treated the disaster lightly;

sentences.zh: 有拙於催科而輿情愛戴者，疏請留任；

translations.literal: where officials were clumsy at tax collection but beloved by public sentiment, he memorialized requesting they be retained;
translations.idiomatic: where officials were poor at tax collection but beloved locally, he asked that they be retained;

sentences.zh: 禁漕幫旂丁陋規。

translations.literal: he forbade the corrupt customs of grain-transport gangs and banner transport workers.
translations.idiomatic: and he banned corrupt customs among grain-transport gangs and banner transport workers.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆末，山東大吏多不得人，吏治日弛。

translations.literal: Since the end of the Qianlong reign, Shandong's high officials had often been unfit, and governance grew lax day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Since the end of the Qianlong reign, Shandong's senior officials had often been unfit and governance had grown lax.

sentences.zh: 大文性深嚴，見屬吏溫顏相對，使盡言，然後正色戒之曰：「汝某事賄若干，吾悉知。

translations.literal: Dawen was by nature deeply stern; when he met subordinate officials he spoke with a gentle face and let them speak fully, then with a stern expression warned them: "You took such-and-such bribes in such-and-such matters—I know them all.
translations.idiomatic: Dawen was deeply stern. He would meet subordinates with a gentle face, let them speak freely, then sternly warn them: "You took such-and-such bribes in such-and-such matters—I know them all.

sentences.zh: 不速改，彈章已具草矣！

translations.literal: If you do not reform quickly, the impeachment memorial is already drafted!
translations.idiomatic: Reform quickly, or the impeachment memorial is already drafted!

sentences.zh: 」人莫不畏之。

translations.literal: No one failed to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 尤銳剔漕弊，杜浮收，官吏被告發劾治者三十餘人。

translations.literal: He was especially sharp in cutting grain-transport abuses, stopping excess collection, and more than thirty officials were impeached and punished after being reported.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially sharp in cutting grain-transport abuses and stopping excess collection; more than thirty officials were impeached after being reported.

sentences.zh: 及去任時，其摘印在系未經奏劾者，尚七八人。

translations.literal: When he left office, those whose seals had been confiscated but who had not yet been memorialized for impeachment still numbered seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, seven or eight officials still had their seals confiscated but had not yet been formally impeached.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，詔布政使分別省釋。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the throne, an edict ordered the provincial treasurer to release them separately according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, the provincial treasurer was ordered to release them case by case.

sentences.zh: 六年，畿輔大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the capital region suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the capital region suffered severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 大文服將闋，特召署直隸總督。

translations.literal: Dawen's mourning was nearly complete when he was specially summoned to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Dawen's mourning was nearly complete when he was specially summoned as acting governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 疏請大賑提早一月，以救災黎。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that major relief be advanced by one month to save the disaster victims.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to advance major relief by one month to save disaster victims.

sentences.zh: 劾查災開賑遲緩之縣令二人，以儆其餘。

translations.literal: He impeached two magistrates for slow disaster inspection and relief opening, to warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached two magistrates for slow disaster inspection and relief, to warn the rest.

sentences.zh: 逾年，因病自乞京職，歷署吏部侍郎、工部尚書。

translations.literal: More than a year later, citing illness, he requested a capital post and served in succession as acting vice minister of personnel and minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, citing illness, he requested a capital post and served as acting vice minister of personnel and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 八年，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiang.

sentences.zh: 劾按察使珠隆阿喜事株累，士民多怨，調珠隆阿內用。

translations.literal: He impeached Provincial Judge Zhulong'a for creating trouble and implicating others, arousing much resentment among scholars and commoners, and Zhulong'a was transferred to an interior post.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Provincial Judge Zhulong'a for creating trouble and implicating others, arousing widespread resentment, and Zhulong'a was transferred inland.

sentences.zh: 江蘇昭文浮收漕糧，江西樂平勒折重徵，縣民並走訴於京，先後下大文鞫實，劾府縣官，褫職究治。

translations.literal: In Jiangsu's Zhaowen there was excess collection of tribute grain; in Jiangxi's Leping there was forced discounting and heavy levies; county people all fled to appeal in the capital; the cases were referred in succession to Dawen, who verified the facts, impeached prefectural and county officials, stripped them of office, and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaowen, Jiangsu, officials over-collected tribute grain; in Leping, Jiangxi, they forced discounts and heavy levies. Villagers appealed to the capital, and Dawen verified both cases, impeached the officials, stripped them of rank, and punished them.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉大文秉公，不徇庇屬員，使小民含冤得白，姦胥猾吏不致幸逃法網，訓責各督撫力改積習。

translations.literal: An edict praised Dawen for acting impartially, not shielding subordinates, allowing common people with grievances to be cleared, and preventing corrupt clerks and crafty officials from escaping the law by luck, and admonished all governors and governors-general to forcefully reform accumulated customs.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Dawen for acting impartially, not shielding subordinates, clearing common people's grievances, and keeping corrupt clerks from escaping justice, and admonished all governors to reform entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 九年，召授左都御史，未至，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned and appointed left censor-in-chief; before he arrived he was promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was summoned as left censor-in-chief; before he arrived he was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 大文赴京，病於途，詔遣侍衛率醫往視，久不痊，賜尚書銜回籍。

translations.literal: Dawen fell ill on the road while traveling to the capital; an edict dispatched a bodyguard leading a physician to attend him; he did not recover for a long time and was granted the ministerial title and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Dawen fell ill en route to the capital; a bodyguard and physician were sent to attend him. He failed to recover and was granted the ministerial title and sent home.

sentences.zh: 既而因在直隸失察屬吏侵挪，部議革職，詔俟病痊以四品京堂用，遂不出。

translations.literal: Later, because he had failed to oversee subordinate officials' embezzlement in Zhili, the ministry proposed dismissal from office; an edict ordered that after recovery he be used as a fourth-rank capital official, but he never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for failing to oversee subordinates' embezzlement in Zhili, dismissal was proposed; the court ordered that after recovery he might serve as a fourth-rank capital official, but he never returned.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 熊枚，字存甫，江西鉛山人。

translations.literal: Xiong Mei, style name Cunfu, was a native of Qianshan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Mei, styled Cunfu, was from Qianshan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十五年，舉鄉試第一，次年，成進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed first in the provincial examination; the next year he became a jinshi and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of the Qianlong reign he placed first in the provincial examination; the next year he became a jinshi and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 斷獄平。

translations.literal: He judged cases fairly.
translations.idiomatic: He judged cases fairly.

sentences.zh: 左翼護軍給餉誤用白片，懼責，私補印，其長當以盜印罪；

translations.literal: A Left Wing Guard pay clerk mistakenly used a blank form, feared punishment, and privately replaced the seal; his superior was liable for the crime of seal theft;
translations.idiomatic: A Left Wing Guard pay clerk mistakenly used a blank form, feared punishment, and privately replaced the seal; his superior faced the capital charge of seal theft;

sentences.zh: 枚謂知誤更正，與盜用異，改緩。

translations.literal: Mei held that knowing the error and correcting it differed from theft of use, and changed the sentence to deferred execution.
translations.idiomatic: Mei held that correcting a known error differed from theft of use and changed the sentence to deferred execution.

sentences.zh: 宜城縣吏毆斃社長，賄改病死，擬緩；

translations.literal: A Yicheng county clerk beat a village head to death, bribed officials to change the cause to illness, and a deferred sentence was proposed;
translations.idiomatic: A Yicheng county clerk beat a village head to death, bribed officials to change the cause to illness, and a deferred sentence was proposed;

sentences.zh: 枚謂鬥毆情輕，舞文情重，改實。

translations.literal: Mei held that the fighting offense was light but the falsification of documents was heavy, and changed it to immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: Mei held that the assault was minor but falsifying documents was grave, and changed the sentence to immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 在部八年，多所持議，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: After eight years in the ministry, with many opinions of his own, he was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in the ministry, often dissenting from precedent, he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 尚書英廉薦其才，出為甘肅平涼知府，母憂去，服闋，補河南汝寧府。

translations.literal: Minister Ying Lian recommended his talent; he went out as prefect of Pingliang in Gansu, left on his mother's death, and after mourning was appointed to Runing Prefecture in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ying Lian recommended his talent; he became prefect of Pingliang in Gansu, left on his mother's death, and after mourning was appointed to Runing Prefecture in Henan.

sentences.zh: 汝陽有殺人獄，已得實，控不止，枚訊鞫時，忽熟視旁吏曰：「此汝所教也！

translations.literal: In Ruyang there was a murder case already judged substantiated, but appeals did not cease; during interrogation Mei suddenly stared closely at a clerk beside him and said: "You taught this!
translations.idiomatic: In Ruyang a murder case had been judged substantiated, but appeals continued. During interrogation Mei suddenly stared at a clerk beside him and said: "You taught this!

sentences.zh: 」吏色變，刑之，則稱將嫁禍某富家，咸以為神。

translations.literal: The clerk's face changed color; under torture he confessed that he had planned to shift blame onto a wealthy family, and all considered it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk's face changed; under torture he confessed he had planned to shift blame onto a wealthy family, and all considered it miraculous.

sentences.zh: 丁生母憂，代者未至，米價騰漲，枚於喪次諭縣令治居奇者，運米接濟，民乃安。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his stepmother before his replacement arrived, rice prices soared; from his mourning quarters Mei instructed the magistrate to punish hoarders, transported rice for relief, and the people were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his stepmother before his replacement arrived, rice prices soared. From his mourning quarters he instructed the magistrate to punish hoarders, brought in rice for relief, and the people were calmed.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補直隸順德府，擢山東泰武臨道。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed to Shunde Prefecture in Zhili and was promoted to intendant of the Taiwu-Lin Circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed prefect of Shunde in Zhili and then promoted to intendant of the Taiwu-Lin Circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，遷江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he was transferred to be Jiangsu provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign, he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 逮治博徒馬修章及竹堂寺僧恆一，皆稔惡骫法者。

translations.literal: He arrested and punished the gambler Ma Xiuzhang and the monk Heng Yi of Zhutang Temple, both long accustomed to wickedness and bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested and punished the gambler Ma Xiuzhang and the monk Heng Yi of Zhutang Temple, both hardened offenders who habitually bent the law.

sentences.zh: 吳江太湖濱淫祠三郎神，奸民所祀，其黨結胥吏擾民。

translations.literal: On the shores of Lake Tai at Wujiang stood a licentious shrine to the Third Lord God, worshipped by ruffians whose faction colluded with clerks to harass the people.
translations.idiomatic: On the shores of Lake Tai at Wujiang stood an illicit shrine to the Third Lord God, maintained by ruffians whose faction colluded with yamen clerks to harass the populace.

sentences.zh: 枚廉知，值賽祠，舟集鶯脰湖，密捕得三十八人，或以誣良訴，尾其舟，得盜贓，並逮劇盜九人，毀三郎像火之，盜遂息。

translations.literal: Mei, having learned of it through his integrity, on the temple festival day when boats gathered on Yingdou Lake secretly captured thirty-eight men; when some sued claiming innocents had been framed, he trailed their boats, recovered stolen goods, also seized nine major bandits, burned the image of the Third Lord, and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the affair through his own investigation, Mei seized the festival day when boats gathered on Yingdou Lake and secretly captured thirty-eight men. When some appealed claiming innocent people had been framed, he trailed their boats, recovered stolen goods, seized nine major bandits as well, burned the image of the Third Lord, and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 教匪劉之協傳彌勒教，入教者給命根錢。

translations.literal: The sect rebel Liu Zhixie propagated the Maitreya teaching; those who entered the sect were given life-root money.
translations.idiomatic: The sect rebel Liu Zhixie spread the Maitreya teaching; initiates were paid so-called life-root money.

sentences.zh: 安徽民任梓家供彌勒像，有簿記六十人奉錢數，官吏捕得，指為匪，巡撫已上聞，逮至江南，枚親訊，六十人皆任梓戚友賀婚嫁者，乃得釋。

translations.literal: An Anhui commoner Ren Zi kept a Maitreya image at home with a register recording sixty people contributing money; officials arrested them and called them rebels; the governor-general had already reported upward; brought to Jiangnan, Mei personally interrogated them and found all sixty were Ren Zi's kin and friends celebrating weddings and marriages, and they were then released.
translations.idiomatic: An Anhui commoner named Ren Zi kept a Maitreya image at home with a ledger listing sixty contributors. Officials arrested them as rebels, and the governor-general had already reported the case. When the detainees were brought to Jiangnan, Mei interrogated them personally and found that all sixty were Ren Zi's relatives and friends attending wedding celebrations, and they were released.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷雲南布政使，以治劉河工未竣，留署江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Yunnan provincial treasurer; because the Liu River works were not yet finished, he was retained as acting Jiangsu provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was appointed provincial treasurer of Yunnan, but because the Liu River project was unfinished he remained as acting provincial treasurer of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 開蘇州城河，集銀六萬兩，擇郡紳董其役，不使縣令與工事。

translations.literal: He opened the Suzhou city canal, raised sixty thousand taels of silver, chose local gentry to direct the project, and did not let magistrates participate in the work.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Suzhou city canal, raised sixty thousand taels, selected leading gentry of the prefecture to supervise the project, and kept county magistrates out of the construction.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，調安徽，尋擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was transferred to Anhui, and soon afterward was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiaqing reign he was transferred to Anhui and soon promoted to vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六年，直隸大水，總督姜晟以辦賑延緩免，命枚署總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year a great flood struck Zhili; Governor Jiang Sheng was dismissed for delay in relief work, and Mei was ordered to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year a great flood struck Zhili. Governor Jiang Sheng was dismissed for slow relief efforts, and Mei was ordered to serve as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 截留漕糧六十萬石儲天津北倉，枚請分儲鄭家口、泊頭諸水次，便災區輓運。

translations.literal: Six hundred thousand shi of tribute grain had been held at the North Granary in Tianjin; Mei requested that it be divided among storage points at Zhengjiakou, Botou, and other depots along the waterways to facilitate transport within the disaster area.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred thousand shi of tribute grain had been held at Tianjin's North Granary. Mei asked that it be split among depots at Zhengjiakou, Botou, and other river stations to ease transport in the stricken region.

sentences.zh: 條上賑恤事宜，災戶仿保甲造冊，省覆查，杜刁控，酌量變通賑期，捐賑者分別旌賞，各學貧生給口糧，綠營兵丁給修房價，修災縣監獄，以工代賑，並如議行。

translations.literal: He submitted detailed relief measures: disaster households were registered on the baojia model, secondary review was reduced, vexatious litigation was blocked, relief periods were adjusted as appropriate, donors were rewarded by degree, poor students at each school were given grain rations, Green Standard troops were given house-repair funds, prisons in affected counties were repaired, relief was given through labor projects, and all was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out relief measures in detail: disaster households were registered like baojia units, redundant review was cut, vexatious suits were blocked, relief schedules were flexibly adjusted, donors were commended by rank, impoverished students received grain allowances, Green Standard soldiers received funds to repair their quarters, county jails in the disaster zone were rebuilt, and work-for-relief projects were adopted—all as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎那彥寶築永定河決口，既而調陳大文為總督，詔枚受代後專任查賑，巡閱數十州縣，舉者五人，劾四人。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Nayenbao he repaired the breach in the Yongding River; afterward Chen Dawen was transferred in as governor, and an edict ordered that after Mei handed over office he should devote himself solely to inspecting relief, touring dozens of prefectures and counties, recommending five men and impeaching four.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Minister Nayenbao he repaired the Yongding River breach. Chen Dawen was then appointed governor, and an edict directed Mei, once he had handed over office, to devote himself entirely to relief inspection, touring dozens of prefectures and counties, recommending five officials and impeaching four.

sentences.zh: 玉田令倪為德清而戇，枚初至，怒之，明日詰賑事，指畫悉中，即首薦。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Yutian, Ni Weide, was honest and blunt; when Mei first arrived he was angry with him, but the next day, questioning him on relief affairs, found every point of his plan sound and immediately recommended him first.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Yutian, Ni Weide, was upright but blunt. Mei was displeased when he first arrived, but the next day, when he questioned him on relief work, found every point of his plan sound and immediately placed him at the top of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 上嘉枚勤事，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Mei's diligence and promoted him to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Mei's diligence and promoted him to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時有劾枚擾驛需索供應者，命陳大文察訪，白其誣，且言枚盡心賑務，特詔褒之。

translations.literal: At the time some impeached Mei for disturbing relay stations and demanding supplies; the emperor ordered Chen Dawen to investigate, who cleared him of the false charge and reported that Mei had devoted himself wholeheartedly to relief; a special edict praised him.
