translations.idiomatic: At the time some officials impeached Mei for harassing relay stations and demanding supplies. The emperor ordered Chen Dawen to investigate; Chen cleared him of the false charge and reported that Mei had given himself entirely to relief work, and a special edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 七年，回京典會試，复署直隸總督，授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned to the capital to preside over the metropolitan examination, again acted as governor of Zhili, and was appointed minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to the capital to preside over the metropolitan examination, again served as acting governor of Zhili, and was appointed minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 調左都御史，管理三庫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left censor-in-chief and placed in charge of the Three Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left censor-in-chief and placed in charge of the Three Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 十年，授工部尚書，復命署直隸總督，率布政使裘行簡清查虧空。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of Works, again ordered to act as governor of Zhili, and led Provincial Treasurer Qiu Xingjian in auditing deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of Works, again ordered to act as governor of Zhili, and led Provincial Treasurer Qiu Xingjian in auditing treasury deficits.

sentences.zh: 部議各省販鐵，官為定額，疏上。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated fixing official quotas for iron sold in each province, and he memorialized upward.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed official quotas for iron trading in each province, and he submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 枚面陳鐵為民間日用所需，不能預定多寡，官為查辦，恐滋流弊。

translations.literal: Mei stated in person that iron was a daily necessity of the people and could not be predetermined in quantity; if officials investigated and managed it, corrupt practices would likely arise.
translations.idiomatic: Mei argued in audience that iron was an everyday necessity for the people and could not be fixed in advance; official supervision would only breed abuse.

sentences.zh: 上俞其說，而斥枚隨同畫諾，召對忽有異詞，年老重聽，不宜部務，復調左都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his view but rebuked Mei for merely going along with others in assent, then suddenly raising different words in audience; he was old and hard of hearing and unfit for ministry duties, and was again transferred to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his argument but rebuked Mei for assenting with others in council only to contradict them in audience; he was elderly, hard of hearing, and unfit for ministry work, and was transferred back to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有山東民婦京控應奏，枚意未決，左副都御史陳嗣龍劾枚模棱，且言枚聲名平常，詔斥嗣龍見枚左遷，揣測妄劾，終以枚不能和衷，鐫級留任。

translations.literal: Before long a Shandong commoner woman appealed to Beijing in a case requiring imperial rescript; Mei had not yet decided; Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Silong impeached Mei for equivocation and also said Mei's reputation was mediocre; an edict rebuked Silong for seeing Mei demoted and impeaching on speculation, but in the end because Mei could not work in harmony his rank was reduced one grade while he was retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a Shandong woman appealed to Beijing in a case requiring an imperial rescript, and Mei had not yet reached a decision. Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Silong impeached him for equivocation and said his reputation was undistinguished. An edict rebuked Silong for impeaching on speculation after Mei's demotion, but in the end Mei was reduced one grade and kept in office because he could not work harmoniously with colleagues.

sentences.zh: 直隸籓司書吏偽印虛收庫銀事覺，坐失察，議褫職，詔以四品京堂用，補順天府丞。

translations.literal: When the Zhili provincial treasurer's clerks' use of forged seals to collect treasury silver falsely came to light, he was punished for lack of supervision; dismissal was proposed, but an edict appointed him to a fourth-rank Beijing post as vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks in the Zhili provincial treasurer's office were found to have used forged seals to collect treasury silver falsely, he was held accountable for lack of supervision. Dismissal was proposed, but an edict appointed him to a fourth-rank Beijing post as vice prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 次年，充鄉試提調官，冊券遲誤，降五品職銜休致。

translations.literal: The next year, serving as chief examiner for the provincial examination, he was late with registers and examination slips and was reduced to fifth-rank honorary status and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while serving as chief examiner for the provincial examinations, he delayed the registers and examination slips and was reduced to fifth-rank honorary status and retired.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 裘行簡，字敬之，江西新建人，尚書曰修子。

translations.literal: Qiu Xingjian, style name Jingzhi, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi, son of Minister Qiu Yuexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Xingjian, styled Jingzhi, was from Xinjian in Jiangxi and was the son of Minister Qiu Yuexiu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年，賜舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he was granted the status of provincial graduate, appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat, served as a clerk on the Grand Council, and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign he was granted provincial graduate status, appointed a Secretariat drafter, served as a Grand Council clerk, and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，從大學士阿桂剿甘肅石峰堡回匪，復從察治河南睢州河工。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he followed Grand Secretary Agui to suppress the Muslim rebels at Shifeng Fort in Gansu, and again followed him to inspect and manage the river works at Suizhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he accompanied Grand Secretary Agui against the Muslim rebels at Shifeng Fort in Gansu and later joined him in inspecting the river works at Suizhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 五十年，出為山西寧武知府，調平陽，因親老，自請改京秩，補戶部員外郎，仍直軍機。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he went out as prefect of Ningwu in Shanxi, was transferred to Pingyang, and because his parents were elderly requested transfer to a Beijing post; he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and still served on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he became prefect of Ningwu in Shanxi and was transferred to Pingyang. When his parents grew old he asked for a capital post, was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and continued on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 累遷太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，命赴陝西犒軍，時經略額勒登保駐略陽，行簡疏言：「川、陝兵宜扼衝嚴守，使陝匪不入川，川匪不入陝，然後逼使東竄，經略以大兵蹙之，可計日梟縛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he was ordered to go to Shaanxi to reward the troops; at the time Commander-in-Chief Eledengbao was stationed at Lueyang. Xingjian memorialized: "Troops of Sichuan and Shaanxi should hold the strategic passes strictly so that Shaanxi rebels do not enter Sichuan and Sichuan rebels do not enter Shaanxi; only then can they be forced eastward, and the commander-in-chief, pressing them with a great army, can capture and bind them within days."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign he was sent to Shaanxi to reward the army while Commander-in-Chief Eledengbao was at Lueyang. Xingjian memorialized: "Sichuan and Shaanxi forces should hold the strategic passes so Shaanxi rebels cannot enter Sichuan and Sichuan rebels cannot enter Shaanxi; only then can they be driven east, and the commander-in-chief, closing in with the main army, can capture them within days."

sentences.zh: 」又言自寶雞至褒城，棧道卡兵宜復設。

translations.literal: "He also said that from Baoji to Baocheng the plank-road checkpoint troops should be re-established."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that checkpoint troops along the plank road from Baoji to Baocheng be restored.

sentences.zh: 且於要害設大營，隔賊路，通糧運。

translations.literal: Moreover, large camps should be set up at key points to block rebel routes and keep grain transport open.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed large camps at critical points to cut rebel routes and secure grain transport.

sentences.zh: 又以額勒登保方引嫌，自請舉劾止及於麾下，行簡疏請五路將士皆聽舉劾，移書川督勒保，陳廉、藺相下之義，兩帥大和。

translations.literal: Because Eledengbao was then avoiding suspicion and had requested that impeachment and recommendation extend only to his own subordinates, Xingjian memorialized asking that officers and soldiers on all five routes be subject to impeachment and recommendation; he wrote to Sichuan Governor Lebao, explaining the principle by which Chen Lian and Lin Xiang deferred to their superiors, and the two commanders were fully reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Eledengbao was then under suspicion and had asked that recommendations and impeachments be limited to his own subordinates. Xingjian memorialized that troops on all five routes should be open to impeachment and recommendation, wrote to Sichuan Governor Lebao on the duty of subordinates such as Chen Lian and Lin Xiang to defer to their superiors, and the two commanders were fully reconciled.

sentences.zh: 途次，進太僕寺卿，賜花翎。

translations.literal: En route he was promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he was promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋出為河南布政使，丁母憂，服闋，補福建布政使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as Henan provincial treasurer; on his mother's death he mourned, and after mourning ended was appointed Fujian provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed provincial treasurer of Henan, left office on his mother's death, and after mourning was appointed provincial treasurer of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆末授受禮成，恩免廢員，各州縣錢穀出入，益滋糾葛，行簡銳事清帑，司冊目十有一，創增子目，支解毫黍皆見，吏不能欺。

translations.literal: From the end of the Qianlong reign, after the succession rites were completed and dismissed officials were pardoned, the receipts and disbursements of each prefecture and county grew ever more entangled in disputes; Xingjian vigorously cleared the treasuries, with eleven main categories in the office registers and newly added subcategories, so that every disbursement down to the smallest fraction was visible and clerks could not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianlong succession, when pardons cleared dismissed officials, county treasury accounts grew ever more tangled. Xingjian drove a thorough cleanup: eleven main ledger categories with new subcategories, so that every disbursement down to the smallest fraction was visible and clerks could not hide fraud.

sentences.zh: 九年，入覲，會仁宗欲清釐直隸倉庫，嘉其成效，特以調任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he came to audience; the Renzong Emperor wished to clear Zhili granaries and treasuries, praised his results, and specially transferred him there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he came to audience just as the Renzong Emperor sought to clear Zhili's granaries and treasuries. Impressed by his results, the emperor transferred him there specially.

sentences.zh: 行簡澈底清覈，逐條覆奏，略曰：「直隸州縣，動以皇差為名，藉口賠累。

translations.literal: Xingjian thoroughly audited and reported item by item, summarizing in part: "Zhili prefectures and counties constantly cite imperial missions as a pretext and plead cumulative losses."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian conducted a thorough audit and reported item by item, writing in part: "Zhili prefectures and counties constantly invoke imperial missions and plead cumulative losses."

sentences.zh: 自乾隆十五年至三十年，四舉南巡，兩幸五台，六次差務，何以並無虧空？

translations.literal: "From the fifteenth to the thirtieth year of Qianlong there were four southern tours, two visits to Wutai, and six rounds of mission expenses—why were there no deficits?"
translations.idiomatic: "From the fifteenth to the thirtieth year of Qianlong there were four southern tours, two visits to Wutai, and six rounds of mission expenses—yet why were there no deficits?"

sentences.zh: 四十五年至五十七年，兩舉南巡，三幸五台，差務較少，​​而虧空日增。

translations.literal: "From the forty-fifth to the fifty-seventh year there were two southern tours and three visits to Wutai, with fewer mission expenses, yet deficits grew daily."
translations.idiomatic: "From the forty-fifth to the fifty-seventh year there were two southern tours and three visits to Wutai, with fewer mission expenses, yet deficits grew daily."

sentences.zh: 由於地方大吏，貪黷營私，結交餽送，非差務之踵事增華，實上司之藉端需索。

translations.literal: "This was because local high officials were greedy and pursued private gain, forming factions and sending gifts; it was not that mission expenses kept escalating in splendor, but that superiors seized pretexts to make demands."
translations.idiomatic: "The cause was greedy local superiors who pursued private gain, formed factions, and sent gifts—not escalating mission extravagance, but superiors using missions as pretexts to extort subordinates."

sentences.zh: 近年一不加察，任其藉詞影射，相習成風。

translations.literal: "In recent years no one has investigated; they have been allowed to use pretexts and shadow charges, and this has become habitual practice."
translations.idiomatic: "In recent years no one has investigated; officials have been allowed to plead pretexts and shadow charges until the practice became habitual."

sentences.zh: 試令州縣捫心自問，其捐官肥己之錢，究從何出？

translations.literal: "Try asking prefectures and counties to search their own hearts: where does the money come from that they spend to buy office and enrich themselves?"
translations.idiomatic: "Let prefectures and counties search their own hearts: where does the money come from that they spend to buy office and enrich themselves?"

sentences.zh: 此臣不敢代為寬解者也。

translations.literal: "On this your servant dares not offer excuses on their behalf."
translations.idiomatic: "On this point your servant dares not offer excuses on their behalf."

sentences.zh: 分年彌補，則有二難：直隸驛務繁多，所有優缺，祗可調劑衝途，又別無陋規可提，此為難一也。

translations.literal: "Making up deficits year by year presents two difficulties: Zhili has numerous relay duties, and all lucrative posts can only be shifted to busy routes, with no corrupt customary fees to draw upon—this is the first difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: "Spreading repayment over years presents two difficulties. Zhili has heavy relay duties, and lucrative posts can only be shifted along busy routes, with no corrupt customary fees to tap—this is the first difficulty."

sentences.zh: 現任虧空，革留勒限，彼必愛惜官職，賣田鬻產，亦思全完。

translations.literal: "For incumbents with deficits, if they are dismissed but retained with a deadline, they will surely value their offices, sell fields and property, and also wish to make full repayment."
translations.idiomatic: "Incumbents with deficits, if dismissed but retained under deadline, will value their posts, sell land and property, and try to make full repayment."

sentences.zh: 若責以代前任按年彌補，焉肯解囊，勢必取給倉庫。

translations.literal: "If they are charged to make up predecessors' deficits year by year, how would they open their purses? They would inevitably take from the granaries and treasuries."
translations.idiomatic: "If they are required to repay predecessors' deficits year by year, they will not open their own purses but inevitably take from county treasuries."

sentences.zh: 前欠未清，後虧復至，此為難二也。

translations.literal: "Former debts unpaid, new deficits recurring—this is the second difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: "Former debts remain unpaid while new deficits appear—this is the second difficulty."

sentences.zh: 州縣虧項無著，例應道府分賠；

translations.literal: "When county deficits cannot be recovered, by regulation circuit intendants and prefects should share compensation;"
translations.idiomatic: "When county deficits cannot be recovered, circuit intendants and prefects should share compensation by regulation;"

sentences.zh: 道府賠項無著，例應院司攤賠。

translations.literal: "when circuit and prefectural compensation cannot be recovered, by regulation provincial treasurers and governors should share it."
translations.idiomatic: "when their compensation cannot be recovered, provincial treasurers and governors should share it by regulation."

sentences.zh: 今直隸未申明定例，請於兩次清查應行監追者，再限一年。

translations.literal: "Zhili has not yet declared the fixed regulations; I request one more year for those who should be supervised and pursued after the two audits."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhili has not yet codified these rules. I ask that those subject to supervision after the two audits be given one more year."

sentences.zh: 如財產實屬盡絕，著落上司分別賠繳。

translations.literal: "If property is truly exhausted, responsibility should be assigned to superiors to compensate by degree."
translations.idiomatic: "If an official's property is truly exhausted, superiors should be assigned to compensate in proportion."

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年以後，交代虧缺，惟有執法從事，不得混入清查，致有寬縱。

translations.literal: "After the tenth year of Jiaqing, deficits on transfer of office must be handled strictly by law and must not be mixed into the general audit, lest leniency result."
translations.idiomatic: "After the tenth year of Jiaqing, deficits discovered on transfer of office must be prosecuted strictly and must not be folded into the general audit, lest offenders be treated leniently."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉其明晰，下部議行。

translations.literal: "When the memorial entered, the emperor praised its clarity and ordered the ministries to deliberate and implement it."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised its clarity and ordered the ministries to deliberate and implement it.

sentences.zh: 尋命以兵部侍郎銜署直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to act as governor of Zhili with the honorary title of vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to serve as acting governor of Zhili with the honorary rank of vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十一年，察出籓司書吏假印虛收解款二十八萬有奇，遣使按訊，歷任總督、布政使議譴有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year it was discovered that clerks in the provincial treasurer's office had used false seals to collect over two hundred and eighty thousand taels of forwarded payments falsely; envoys were sent to investigate, and successive governors and provincial treasurers were censured to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year clerks in the provincial treasurer's office were found to have used forged seals to collect more than two hundred and eighty thousand taels in forwarded payments falsely. Investigators were dispatched, and successive governors and provincial treasurers were censured to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 行簡任內虛收之數少，詔以事由行簡立法清查，始得發覺，寬之。

translations.literal: The amount falsely collected during Xingjian's tenure was small; an edict held that because Xingjian had established regulations for a thorough audit the affair had come to light, and he was leniently treated.
translations.idiomatic: The amount falsely collected during Xingjian's tenure was small. An edict noted that his regulations for thorough audit had exposed the fraud, and he was treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，赴永定河勘工，途次感疾，卒。

translations.literal: That autumn, while going to inspect works on the Yongding River, he fell ill on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, while traveling to inspect Yongding River works, he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 上深惜之，優詔賜卹依一品例，諡恭勤，賜子元善舉人。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it, issued a generous edict of condolence according to first-rank precedent, posthumously titled him Gongqin ("Respectful and Diligent"), and granted his son Yuanshan the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted his loss, issued a generous condolence edict on the precedent for first rank, gave him the posthumous title Gongqin, and granted his son Yuanshan provincial graduate status.

sentences.zh: 方維甸，字南耦，安徽桐城人，總督觀承子。

translations.literal: Fang Weidian, style name Nan'ou, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui, son of Governor Fang Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Weidian, styled Nan'ou, was from Tongcheng in Anhui and was the son of Governor Fang Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 觀承年逾六十，始生維甸。

translations.literal: Guancheng was over sixty before Weidian was born.
translations.idiomatic: Guancheng was past sixty when Weidian was born.

sentences.zh: 高宗命抱至御前，解佩囊賜之。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor ordered him carried before the imperial presence and bestowed his own purse pouch.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor had him brought before the throne and bestowed his own purse pouch.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，帝巡幸山東，維甸以貢生迎駕，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, when the emperor toured Shandong, Weidian as a tribute student welcomed the imperial procession, was appointed a Secretariat drafter, and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of the Qianlong reign, when the emperor toured Shandong, Weidian as a tribute student welcomed the imperial procession, was appointed a Secretariat drafter, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，成進士，授吏部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and rose through the ranks to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，從福康安徵台灣，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he followed Fuk'anggan on the Taiwan campaign and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he followed Fuk'anggan on the Taiwan campaign and was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，累擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and promoted by stages to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the censorate and promoted by stages to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又從福康安徵廓爾喀。

translations.literal: He again followed Fuk'anggan on the Gurkha campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Fuk'anggan on the Gurkha campaign.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺卿、太常寺卿，授長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: He served as minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was appointed Changlu salt controller.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was appointed Changlu salt controller.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，坐事奪職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 吏議遣戍軍台，詔寬免，降刑部員外郎，仍直軍機。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel proposed banishment to the military penal colony; an edict granted leniency, reduced him to vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and he still served on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel proposed banishment to the military penal colony. An edict granted leniency, reduced him to vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and he continued on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從尚書那彥成治陝西軍務。

translations.literal: He followed Minister Nayancheng in managing Shaanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister Nayancheng in managing military affairs in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，授山東按察使，遷河南布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Shandong provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to Henan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Shandong and transferred to provincial treasurer of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時川、楚教匪未靖，維甸率兵六千防守江岸。

translations.literal: At the time the Sichuan and Hubei sect rebels were not yet pacified; Weidian led six thousand troops to guard the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan and Hubei sect rebels were not yet pacified. Weidian led six thousand troops to guard the Yangzi bank.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「大功將蕆，裁撤鄉勇，最為要務。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The great achievement is about to be concluded; disbanding the local militia is the most important task."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "With the great victory nearly complete, disbanding the local militia is the most urgent task."

sentences.zh: 宜在撤兵之前，預為籌議。

translations.literal: "This should be planned in advance, before troops are withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: "Planning should begin before regular troops are withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 俟陝西餘匪殄盡，酌移河南防兵以易勇，可節省勇糧。

translations.literal: "After the remaining rebels in Shaanxi are exterminated, Henan garrison troops may be shifted in proportion to replace the militia, saving militia grain costs."
translations.idiomatic: "Once remaining rebels in Shaanxi are eliminated, Henan garrison troops can be shifted proportionally to replace the militia and save militia grain costs."

sentences.zh: 」上韙之。

translations.literal: "The emperor approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，調陝西，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shaanxi and was immediately promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shaanxi and immediately promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 督捕南山零匪，籌撤鄉勇，覈治糧餉，並協機宜，复賜花翎。

translations.literal: He supervised the pursuit of scattered rebels in the southern mountains, planned the disbanding of militia, audited grain pay, and coordinated strategy; he was again granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He directed pursuit of scattered rebels in the southern mountains, planned militia disbandment, audited grain supplies, and coordinated strategy, and was again granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十一年，寧陝新兵叛，維甸亟令總兵楊芳馳回，偕提督楊遇春進山督剿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the new troops of Ningshan mutinied; Weidian urgently ordered Regional Commander Yang Fang to ride back, and together with Provincial Commander Yang Yuchun entered the mountains to direct suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Ningshan new troops mutinied. Weidian urgently ordered Regional Commander Yang Fang to return at once and joined Provincial Commander Yang Yuchun in entering the mountains to direct suppression.

sentences.zh: 會德楞泰奉命視師，賊竄兩河，將趨石泉，維甸遣總兵王兆夢擊之，勸民修寨自衛，賊無所掠。

translations.literal: When Delin arrived by imperial command to take command, the rebels fled between the two rivers and were about to move toward Shiquan; Weidian sent Regional Commander Wang Zhaomeng to strike them and urged the people to fortify stockades for self-defense, so the rebels had nothing to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When Delingtai arrived to take command, the rebels fled between the Han and Wei rivers and were heading toward Shiquan. Weidian sent Regional Commander Wang Zhaomeng to strike them and urged the people to fortify stockades, leaving the rebels nothing to plunder.

sentences.zh: 未幾，叛兵乞降，德楞泰請以蒲大芳等二百餘人仍歸原伍。

translations.literal: Before long the mutineers begged to surrender; Delingtai requested that more than two hundred men including Pu Dafang be returned to their original units.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the mutineers sought to surrender. Delingtai asked that more than two hundred men including Pu Dafang be returned to their original units.

sentences.zh: 上責其寬縱，命維甸按治，疏陳善後六事，如議行。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked this as lenient and ordered Weidian to investigate and punish; he memorialized six measures for subsequent order, and all were implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked this as too lenient and ordered Weidian to investigate and punish. He memorialized six measures for subsequent order, and all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 蔡牽甫殲，硃渥乞降，遣散餘眾。

translations.literal: Cai Qian had just been destroyed; Zhu Wo begged to surrender, and the remaining followers were dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qian had just been destroyed. Zhu Wo surrendered, and the remaining followers were dispersed.

sentences.zh: 台灣嘉義、彰化二縣械鬥，命往按治，獲犯林聰等，論如律。

translations.literal: Armed clashes broke out in Jiayi and Zhanghua prefectures in Taiwan; he was ordered to investigate and punish, captured the culprits Lin Cong and others, and sentenced them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Armed clashes broke out in Jiayi and Zhanghua in Taiwan. He was ordered to investigate, captured offenders including Lin Cong, and sentenced them according to law.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「台灣屯務廢弛，派員查勘，卹番丁苦累，申明班兵舊制，及歸併營汛地，以便操防；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Taiwan garrison land administration has fallen into neglect; officers should be sent to survey it, relieve the burdens of the native levies, clarify the old system for garrison soldiers, and merge garrison zones with military land to facilitate training and defense;"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Taiwan's garrison land administration has fallen into neglect. Officers should be sent to survey holdings, relieve burdens on native levies, restore the old system for garrison soldiers, and merge garrison zones with military land to ease training and defense;"

sentences.zh: 約束台民械鬥，設約長、族長，令管本莊、本族，嚴禁隸役黨護把持；

translations.literal: "to restrain armed clashes among Taiwanese commoners, establish covenant heads and clan heads to govern their own villages and clans, and strictly forbid yamen runners and factions from shielding and controlling affairs;"
translations.idiomatic: "to curb armed clashes among Taiwanese commoners by appointing covenant heads and clan heads to govern their own villages and clans, and strictly forbid yamen runners and factions from shielding offenders;"

sentences.zh: 又商船貿易口岸，牌照不符，定三口通行章程，杜丁役句串舞弊。

translations.literal: "and for merchant vessels trading at ports where licenses did not match, fix regulations for passage at three ports to block collusion and fraud by runners."
translations.idiomatic: "and for merchant vessels whose licenses did not match trading ports, establish regulations for passage at three ports to stop collusion and fraud by runners."

sentences.zh: 」詔皆允行。

translations.literal: "Edicts approved all measures."
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all of these measures.

sentences.zh: 以台俗民悍，命總督、將軍每二年親赴巡查一次，著為例。

translations.literal: Because the customs of Taiwan made the people fierce, the governor-general and the regional commander were ordered to go in person to inspect once every two years, and this was established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taiwan's customs made the people fierce, the governor-general and regional commander were ordered to inspect in person every two years, and this was made precedent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，入覲，以母老乞終養，允之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he came to audience; because his mother was elderly he begged to retire and care for her permanently, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he came to audience. His mother was elderly, and he begged to retire and care for her permanently; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 會浙江巡撫蔣攸銛疏劾鹽政弊混，命維甸按治。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang Governor Jiang Youqian memorialized impeaching confusion in salt administration, Weidian was ordered to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang Governor Jiang Youqian memorialized exposing confusion in salt administration, Weidian was ordered to investigate and punish.

sentences.zh: 明年，召授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned and appointed a Grand Council minister.

sentences.zh: 維甸疏陳母病，請寢前命，允其留籍侍養。

translations.literal: Weidian memorialized that his mother was ill and begged that the previous order be suspended; he was allowed to remain in his native place to serve her.
translations.idiomatic: Weidian memorialized that his mother was ill and asked that the appointment be set aside. He was allowed to remain at home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 十八年，丁母憂，遣江寧將軍奠醊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered mourning for his mother; the Jiangning regional commander was sent to offer sacrificial libations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he entered mourning for his mother, and the Jiangning regional commander was sent to offer sacrificial libations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，教匪林清謀逆，李文成據滑縣，奪情起署直隸總督，維甸自請馳赴軍營勦賊，會那彥成督師奏捷，允維甸回籍守制。

translations.literal: Before long the sect rebel Lin Qing plotted rebellion and Li Wencheng seized Huaxian; Weidian was recalled from mourning to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili; he volunteered to rush to the army camps to suppress the rebels; Nayancheng, commanding the army, reported victory, and Weidian was allowed to return home to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward sect rebel Lin Qing plotted rebellion while Li Wencheng seized Huaxian. Weidian was recalled from mourning as acting governor-general of Zhili and volunteered to rush to the camps. When Nayancheng reported victory, Weidian was allowed to return home and complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 上以維甸忠誠清慎，深惜之，贈太子少保，諡勤襄，賜其子傳穆進士。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Weidian loyal, sincere, and scrupulous, deeply regretted his loss, granted him the posthumous title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave him the temple name Qinxiang, and granted his son Chuanmu the rank of jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted the loss of so loyal and scrupulous a man, granted him the posthumous title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with temple name Qinxiang, and made his son Chuanmu a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 董教增，字益甫，江蘇上元人。

translations.literal: Dong Jiaozeng, style name Yifu, was a native of Shangyuan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jiaozeng, styled Yifu, was from Shangyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年，南巡，召試舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he was summoned to examination as a provincial graduate and appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of the Qianlong reign, during the southern tour, he was examined as a provincial graduate and appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，成一甲三名進士，授編修，散館改吏部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he became a jinshi of the third rank in the first class, was appointed a Hanlin compiler, and after leaving the academy was transferred to a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, rising by stages to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he placed third in the first class of the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin compiler, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，以道員發四川，明年，授按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was dispatched to Sichuan as a circuit intendant; the next year he was appointed provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he was sent to Sichuan as a circuit intendant and the next year became provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 瓘眉、雷波二廳銅鉛各廠，毗連夷地。

translations.literal: The copper and lead works of the two subprefectures of Jianmei and Leibo bordered Yi territory.
translations.idiomatic: The copper and lead works at the subprefectures of Jianmei and Leibo bordered Yi territory.

sentences.zh: 奸民與爭界，焚夷巢，倮夷糾涼山生番為變，教增率兵往，議者多主剿，教增不可，廉得漢奸構釁者十一人，夷匪首事者六人，集眾誅之，夷情帖然。

translations.literal: Wicked men disputed the border, burned Yi stockades, and the Luo Yi rallied Liangshan aborigines in revolt. Jiaozeng led troops there; many advisers favored extermination, but he refused, investigated and found eleven Han Chinese who had provoked trouble and six Yi ringleaders, gathered the people and executed them, and the Yi submitted peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men disputed the border and burned Yi stockades; the Luo Yi rallied Liangshan aborigines in revolt. Jiaozeng led troops there while many advisers favored extermination, but he refused. He found eleven Han provocateurs and six Yi ringleaders, had them executed, and the Yi submitted peacefully.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以教增不煩兵力，而遠夷心服，諭獎有加。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor, because Jiaozeng had not troubled military force yet won the hearts of distant barbarians, issued edicts of special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor commended him especially for winning over distant tribes without troubling the army.

sentences.zh: 尋調貴州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷四川布政使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became provincial treasurer of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 寧國、池州、廣德各屬，舊有棚民，植雜糧為業。

translations.literal: In the dependencies of Ningguo, Chizhou, and Guangde there were formerly shed-dwellers who planted miscellaneous grains for a living.
translations.idiomatic: In the dependencies of Ningguo, Chizhou, and Guangde, shed-dwellers had long planted miscellaneous grains for a living.

sentences.zh: 戶部慮妨民田，議遣回籍。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue feared harm to civilian fields and proposed sending them back to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue feared harm to civilian fields and proposed sending them home.

sentences.zh: 教增言：「棚民既立室家，難復遷徙。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng said: "The shed-dwellers have already established households and families; it would be hard to move them again.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng said: "The shed-dwellers have already established families; moving them again would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 且所種多隙壤，於民田無損，於民食有益，第約束之而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, what they plant is mostly marginal soil, which does no harm to civilian fields and benefits the people's food supply—they need only be regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they mostly plant marginal soil, which harms no civilian fields and helps feed the people—they need only be regulated.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「徽、寧等府巨室，向有世僕，出戶已久，告訐頻仍，請嚴杜妄訟，凡世僕以現在是否服役為斷；

translations.literal: He also said: "In Huizhou, Ningguo, and other prefectures great households formerly had hereditary bondservants who left the household long ago, yet lawsuits are frequent; please strictly stop false litigation, and decide all cases of hereditary bondservants by whether they are presently in service;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In Huizhou, Ningguo, and other prefectures, great households once held hereditary bondservants who left service long ago, yet lawsuits remain frequent. False litigation should be stopped, and cases decided by whether bondservants are presently in service;

sentences.zh: 其出戶及百年者，雖有據亦開豁為良。

translations.literal: those who left the household or whose departure dates back a century, even if they have documentation, should also be released to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: those who left service or whose departure dates back a century should be released to commoner status even if documentation exists.

sentences.zh: 」得旨允行，著為例。

translations.literal: An edict approved and made it a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved and made it a precedent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，調陝西。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 興安七屬，舊食河東引鹽。

translations.literal: The seven dependencies of Xing'an formerly consumed salt under the Hedong distribution system.
translations.idiomatic: The seven dependencies of Xing'an had long consumed salt under the Hedong distribution system.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，課攤地丁，其後復歸商運。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign the levy was spread over land and poll taxes; afterward it reverted to merchant transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign the levy was spread over land and poll taxes, then reverted to merchant transport.

sentences.zh: 地介川、楚，土鹽侵礙，運艱費重，引課多虧。

translations.literal: The region bordered Sichuan and Huguang; local salt encroached, transport was difficult and costly, and distribution revenues often ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering Sichuan and Huguang, local salt encroached, transport was costly, and distribution revenues often fell short.

sentences.zh: 教增請循鳳翔例，改食花馬池鹽，引歸民運，課按丁攤，以卹商力。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng requested following the Fengxiang precedent, changing consumption to Huamachi salt, returning distribution to civilian transport, and spreading the levy by household to relieve merchant burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng asked to follow the Fengxiang precedent: switch to Huamachi salt, return transport to civilians, and spread the levy by household to relieve merchants.

sentences.zh: 又榆林、綏德、吳堡、米脂四州縣，向食土鹽，官給票銷售。

translations.literal: In the four prefectures and counties of Yulin, Suide, Wubu, and Mizhi, they had long consumed local salt sold under official tickets.
translations.idiomatic: In Yulin, Suide, Wubu, and Mizhi, locals had long consumed native salt sold under official tickets.

sentences.zh: 前撫方維甸請用部引，以二百斤為率，凡萬一千三百餘引，民力難勝。

translations.literal: The former governor Fang Weidian had requested using ministry distribution certificates at two hundred jin per certificate, totaling more than eleven thousand three hundred certificates—beyond what the people could bear.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor Fang Weidian had required ministry distribution certificates at two hundred jin each, totaling more than eleven thousand three hundred certificates—more than the people could bear.

sentences.zh: 教增規復其舊，由州縣頒發小票，每票五十斤，民皆便之。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng restored the old practice: prefectures and counties issued small tickets of fifty jin each, and the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng restored the old practice of small county tickets at fifty jin each, which the people found convenient.

sentences.zh: 時南山善後倚漢中知府嚴如熤，能盡其才，不拘文法，歲歉請賑，逾限破例，上陳得允。

translations.literal: At that time post-rebellion work in the southern mountains relied on Hanzhong Prefect Yan Ruyi, who could fully use his talents, was not bound by formal regulations, and when famine struck requested relief beyond the deadline and broke precedent—the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: Post-rebellion work in the southern mountains relied on Hanzhong Prefect Yan Ruyi, who used his talents freely, ignored formal regulations, and when famine struck secured approval for relief beyond the deadline.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 先是百齡銳意滅海寇，曾貽教增詩云：「嶺南一事君堪羨，殺賊歸來啖荔支。

translations.literal: Earlier Bailing was keen to exterminate sea pirates and once sent Jiaozeng a poem: "In Lingnan there is one matter you may envy—kill the bandits and return to eat lychees.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bailing was keen to exterminate pirates and once sent Jiaozeng a poem: "In Lingnan there is one thing to envy—kill the bandits and return to eat lychees.

sentences.zh: 」既而張保仔就撫，教增報書曰：「詩應改一字為『降』賊歸來也。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Baozi surrendered; Jiaozeng replied: "The poem should change one character to 'surrendered' bandits returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Baozi surrendered, Jiaozeng replied: "The poem should change one word to 'surrendered' bandits returning.

sentences.zh: 」百齡愧之；

translations.literal: Bailing was ashamed;
translations.idiomatic: Bailing was embarrassed;

sentences.zh: 至是承其後，諸降人桀驁，為閭閻害，懲治甚力，然未嘗妄殺。

translations.literal: now he succeeded him; the various surrendered men were arrogant and harmed neighborhoods, and he punished them severely yet never killed recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: now he succeeded him. Surrendered men were arrogant and harmed neighborhoods; he punished them severely but never killed recklessly.

sentences.zh: 廣州府有死囚，值赦減等改軍而逃，獲之，論重闢，按察使持之堅，教增以律不當死，龂龂與辯，此囚卒免死。

translations.literal: In Guangzhou Prefecture a condemned prisoner, when an amnesty reduced his sentence to military exile, escaped; when captured he was sentenced to severe execution; the provincial judge held firm, but Jiaozeng argued the law did not warrant death and debated stubbornly—the prisoner was ultimately spared.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzhou a condemned prisoner escaped after an amnesty reduced his sentence to military exile. The provincial judge insisted on severe execution, but Jiaozeng argued the law did not warrant death and debated stubbornly until the prisoner was spared.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先是海寇未平，禁商​​民造船高不得逾一丈八尺，小不任重載，難涉風濤，沿海多失業。

translations.literal: Earlier, while sea pirates were not yet pacified, merchants and commoners were forbidden to build vessels higher than one zhang eight chi; the boats were too small to bear heavy loads or weather storms, and many along the coast lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while pirates were still active, merchants were forbidden to build vessels over one zhang eight chi high. The boats were too small for heavy loads or rough seas, and many coastal people lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 教增以寇平已久，請免立禁限，以從民便，允之。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng, considering that piracy had long been pacified, requested abolishing the prohibition for the people's convenience, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng argued that piracy had long been pacified and asked to abolish the restriction for the people's convenience; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 福清武生林彌高者，健訟包糧，阻眾不納，邑令躬緝，為其黨邀奪，官役並傷，令文武往捕獲，彌高嗾其黨劫持，通縣抗徵。

translations.literal: In Fuqing there was a military licentiate named Lin Migao who was skilled at litigation and monopolized grain collection, blocking the people from paying; the magistrate went in person to arrest him, was ambushed and robbed by his faction, and clerks and runners were injured; civil and military officials went to capture him; Migao incited his faction to seize hostages, and the whole county resisted tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: In Fuqing, military licentiate Lin Migao was skilled at litigation and monopolized grain collection, blocking payment. The magistrate went to arrest him in person but was ambushed by his faction and clerks were injured. When officials captured him, Migao incited his followers to seize hostages and the whole county resisted taxes.

sentences.zh: 教增親鞫得彌高罪狀，立斬以徇，諸郡慴懼，強宗悍族抗欠者，皆輸納如額。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng personally tried him, established Migao's guilt, and had him executed immediately as a warning; all prefectures were awed, and powerful clans and fierce families who resisted payment all paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng personally tried him, established his guilt, and executed him immediately as a warning. All prefectures were awed, and powerful clans who had resisted payment paid in full.

sentences.zh: 奏入，詔嘉其能。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, an edict praised his capability.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his capability.

sentences.zh: 臨海民糾眾毆差，致釀大獄。

translations.literal: People in Linhai banded together to beat government runners, producing a major case.
translations.idiomatic: In Linhai, people banded together to beat government runners, producing a major case.

sentences.zh: 巡撫楊頀坐褫職，命教增兼權浙撫，鞫治之。

translations.literal: Governor Yang Hui was stripped of office for it; Jiaozeng was ordered to act concurrently as Zhejiang governor and conduct the trial.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yang Hui was stripped of office; Jiaozeng was ordered to act as Zhejiang governor and conduct the trial.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉兩郡多械鬥殺人，官吏往往不能制。

translations.literal: In the two prefectures of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou armed feuds and killings were frequent, and officials often could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangzhou and Quanzhou armed feuds and killings were frequent, and officials often could not control them.

sentences.zh: 龍溪令姚瑩捕渠魁五人，杖斃之。

translations.literal: Longxi Magistrate Yao Ying captured five ringleaders and beat them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi Magistrate Yao Ying captured five ringleaders and beat them to death.

sentences.zh: 巡撫疑其違制，教增曰：「刑亂國宜用重典。

translations.literal: The governor suspected violation of regulations; Jiaozeng said: "In punishing a disorderly state one should use severe statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The governor suspected a violation of regulations. Jiaozeng said: "In a disorderly region one should use severe statutes.

sentences.zh: 」優容之，悍俗稍戢。

translations.literal: He was indulged, and the fierce customs subsided somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was indulged, and the fierce local customs subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 張保仔就撫後，改名寶，官至澎湖副將，時論猶指斥。

translations.literal: After Zhang Baozi surrendered he changed his name to Bao, rose to deputy commander at Penghu, and public opinion still denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Baozi surrendered he changed his name to Bao, rose to deputy commander at Penghu, and public opinion still denounced him.

sentences.zh: 教增責令捕盜，奔走海上，盜平而寶亦死。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng ordered him to capture pirates and race about the sea; when piracy was pacified Bao also died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng ordered him to hunt pirates at sea; when piracy ended, Bao died as well.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，入覲，乞病未允，道光元年，乃得請歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he entered audience and begged leave for illness without success; in the first year of Daoguang he was finally allowed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he entered audience and asked to retire for illness without success; in the first year of the Daoguang reign he was finally allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，賜卹，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the second year he died; funeral gifts were granted and he was given the temple name Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died; funeral gifts were granted and he received the temple name Wenge.

sentences.zh: 教增有識量，強毅不阿。

translations.literal: Jiaozeng had judgment and breadth of view, was strong and resolute, and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozeng had judgment and breadth of view, was strong and resolute, and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 官四川時，力矯豪奢，崇節儉，宴集不設劇。

translations.literal: When he served in Sichuan he forcefully corrected extravagance, honored thrift, and held banquets without theatrical performances.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan he forcefully corrected extravagance, honored thrift, and held banquets without theatrical performances.

sentences.zh: 總督勒保以春酒召，聞樂而返；

translations.literal: Governor-General Lebao invited him with spring wine; hearing music he turned back;
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lebao invited him for spring wine; hearing music, he turned back;

sentences.zh: 亟撤樂，乃至，盡歡。

translations.literal: the music was quickly removed, and only then did he come and enjoy the feast fully.
translations.idiomatic: the music was quickly removed, and only then did he come and enjoy the feast.

sentences.zh: 嘗言「刻於己為儉，儉於人為刻」，時嘆為名言。

translations.literal: He once said, "Being strict with oneself is thrift; being thrifty with others is harshness," and contemporaries praised it as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Being strict with oneself is thrift; being thrifty with others is harshness," and contemporaries praised it as a famous saying.

sentences.zh: 論曰：吳熊光忠讜任重，有大臣風。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wu Xiongguang was loyal and outspoken, bore heavy responsibility, and had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wu Xiongguang was loyal and outspoken, bore heavy responsibility, and had the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 汪志伊、陳大文矜尚廉厲，或矯或偏。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiyi and Chen Dawen prized integrity and severity, yet one was affected and the other partial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyi and Chen Dawen prized integrity and severity, yet one was affected and the other partial.

sentences.zh: 熊枚勤於民事，晚誚模棱。

translations.literal: Xiong Mei was diligent in civilian affairs but in his later years was mocked for equivocation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Mei was diligent in civilian affairs but in his later years was mocked for equivocation.

sentences.zh: 名位雖皆不終，要為當時佼佼。

translations.literal: Though their fame and rank did not all reach completion, they were nevertheless the outstanding men of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Though none fully reached the heights of fame and rank, they were nevertheless among the outstanding men of their time.

sentences.zh: 裘行簡、方維甸，名父之子，特被恩知。

translations.literal: Qiu Xingjian and Fang Weidian were sons of famous fathers and were specially favored with imperial trust.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Xingjian and Fang Weidian were sons of famous fathers and enjoyed special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 董教增有為有守，建樹閎達，蓋無間然。

translations.literal: Dong Jiaozeng was capable and principled, his achievements broad and far-reaching, and on the whole beyond reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jiaozeng was capable and principled, his achievements broad and far-reaching, and on the whole beyond reproach.
